regulation.binding_note: No binding instrument of any kind addresses AI systems, models or outputs.
regulation.summary: Afghanistan under the Islamic Emirate has no AI-specific legislation, decree or draft instrument, and no sectoral AI rules. Pre-2021 general instruments such as the Cyber Crime Law (2017) contain no provisions written for AI systems, and the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology has issued no AI governance measure while the state itself deploys AI-enabled CCTV and facial-recognition surveillance in Kabul without a legal framework.

ALB.name: Albania

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding act is in force, Council of Ministers Decision No. 479/2024 on AI methodology and technical standards for public bodies.
regulation.summary: Albania has no AI statute in force; the one binding AI-specific instrument is Council of Ministers Decision No. 479, dated 24 July 2024, approving a methodology and technical standards for AI use in the Republic of Albania, which reaches public institutions only. A full draft Law 'On Artificial Intelligence' of 106 articles in 9 chapters, transposing Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, was published by AKSHI for public consultation from 29 May to 26 June 2026 and is not yet enacted. AI systems otherwise fall under Law No. 124/2024 on Personal Data Protection and Law No. 25/2024 on Cybersecurity, which contain no AI-specific provisions.

promotion.note: AKSHI runs an AI Laboratory and tendered EUR 2.6 million for AI-assisted acquis transposition; regulatory sandboxes exist only in the unadopted draft AI law.

DZA.name: Algeria

regulation.binding_note: The only binding instruments reaching AI are general: Law No. 25-11 (2025) on personal data protection and Presidential Decree No. 26-07 (2026) on information-system security units.
regulation.summary: Algeria governs AI through the non-binding National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2024), whose six pillars include a future regulatory framework that has not been drafted into legislation. Binding obligations touching AI come only from general instruments — Law No. 25-11 amending Law No. 18-07 on personal data protection and the cybersecurity decrees — none of which is written for AI systems. Activity in 2026 was institutional: the Prime Minister reviewed strategy progress on 25 May 2026, an interministerial follow-up commission was installed on 5 August 2026, and five thematic commissions on data and infrastructure, financing, large language models, AI doctoral training and continuing AI education were installed on 8 September 2026.

promotion.note: Algérie Télécom's 1.5 billion dinar investment in AI, cybersecurity and robotics startups and the planned national AI and data research centre announced 8 September 2026 constitute funding programs…

AND.name: Andorra

regulation.binding_note: One AI-written binding provision exists, the deepfake sexual-image offence in the Codi penal reform adopted 15 July 2026.
regulation.summary: Andorra has no dedicated AI statute; AI is addressed through adapted general law, principally the Penal Code reform approved on 15 July 2026, which criminalises AI-generated non-consensual sexual imagery, and the Llei 29/2021 de protecció de dades personals as amended by Llei 12/2024. The Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence (CETS 225), signed on 5 September 2024, remains unratified, and the February 2024 Codi d'Ètica de la Intel·ligència Artificial is voluntary.

promotion.note: The Programa de Digitalització d'Empreses 2026 disbursed its full €500,000 to 178 firms for cloud, big data and AI solutions; no AI sandbox or AI procurement rules exist.

AGO.name: Angola

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument is in force; Personal Data Protection Law No. 22/11 and Law No. 6/26 reach AI through general disinformation and data rules.
regulation.summary: Angola's horizontal AI framework remains a bill: the MINTTICS Proposta de Lei sobre Inteligência Artificial, presented in September 2025 with risk-based classification, strict liability, mandatory watermarking and extraterritorial reach, obtained general approval in the National Assembly but has not been enacted. The only binding rules touching AI in force are in Law No. 6/26 Against False Information on the Internet, promulgated 21 July 2026 and published 4 August 2026, which defines deepfakes and artificial dissemination networks and imposes platform duties for that content type. A revised Personal Data Protection Law containing a chapter on data processing by artificial intelligence systems went through public consultation in 2025 and is still pending.

promotion.note: No funded AI programme, AI procurement rule or regulatory sandbox operates; activity is limited to a startup bill approved in general terms in March 2026 and cooperation agreements.

ATG.name: Antigua and Barbuda

regulation.binding_note: Only general law applies, principally the Data Protection Act, 2013 (No. 10 of 2013); no AI-specific binding instrument exists.
regulation.summary: No AI-specific legislation is in force and no AI bill is before Parliament, although the Prime Minister has confirmed that draft AI legislation has been prepared. Governance of AI-related harms rests on the Data Protection Act, 2013 and the Electronic Crimes Act, 2013, which contain no provisions written for AI; the UNESCO Artificial Intelligence Readiness Assessment Report launched on 24 June 2025 identifies modernisation of these frameworks, including impact assessments for high-risk applications, as an outstanding gap.

promotion.note: Project Optimus AI-enhanced border management and a planned government data centre with AI capacity announced in September 2026 involve no regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules.

ATG.key_laws: Data Protection Act, 2013 (No. 10 of 2013), Electronic Crimes Act, 2013, UNESCO Artificial Intelligence Readiness Assessment Report for Antigua and Barbuda (2025), Santiago Declaration on Ethical AI (2023)

ARG.name: Argentina

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: Personal Data Protection Law 25.326 (2000) and sectoral rules such as BCRA Comunicación A 7724, with no binding AI-specific instrument in force.
regulation.summary: Argentina has no enacted binding AI-specific legislation at national level; the Personal Data Protection Law 25.326 (2000) remains the operative instrument, supplemented by Disposición AAIP 2/2023 on Recommendations for Reliable Artificial Intelligence and SIGEN Resolución 197/2026 approving an AI control guide for public-sector internal audit. Several AI bills are before Congress, including the framework bill that obtained a majority committee dictamen in the Chamber of Deputies and the Executive's May 2026 bill creating AI-operated corporate forms, while President Milei has publicly committed to keeping AI development free of preventive regulation. Coverage of private-sector or high-risk AI uses rests on general data-protection, consumer and sectoral rules.

promotion.note: Resolución 90/2021 created an AI capacity-building programme and the Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones (Law 27.742, extended by Decreto 105/2026) channels investment into AI data…

ARM.name: Armenia

regulation.binding_note: Only general instruments reach AI: the Law on Personal Data Protection (No. 49-ZR) and the Law on Cybersecurity in force since 4 January 2026.
regulation.summary: No domestic AI-specific binding instrument exists; the only binding AI text touching Armenia is the Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (STCE n°225), signed on 27 January 2026 and not yet ratified. AI appears in national law only through the August 2026 amendment to the Law on the Structure and Activities of the Government, which renamed the Ministry of High-Tech Industry as the Ministry of High-Tech Industry and Artificial Intelligence and gave it responsibility for AI and cloud computing policy. General instruments such as the Law on Personal Data Protection and the Law on Cybersecurity, in force since 4 January 2026, contain no provision written for AI.

AUS.name: Australia

regulation.binding_note: The only AI-specific binding instrument applying today is the set of Phase 2 online safety codes covering generative AI services; the Privacy Act ADM obligation applies from 10 December 2026.
regulation.summary: Australia has no AI Act: the National AI Plan of 2 December 2025 confirmed reliance on existing laws and sector regulators instead of the 2024 mandatory guardrails proposal, and the Prime Minister's 15 July 2026 announcement of legislated Australian Standards for AI, endorsed by National Cabinet on 26 August 2026, targets legislation in early 2027 starting with large data centres and model training inputs. Binding AI obligations in force are domain-specific: the eSafety Age-Restricted Material Codes (effective 9 March 2026) impose age-assurance duties on generative AI and AI companion services, and the Digital Transformation Agency's Policy for the responsible use of AI in government binds 94 non-corporate Commonwealth entities. The cross-sector automated decision-making transparency obligation added to Australian Privacy Principle 1 by the Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024 commences 10 December 2026.

AUT.name: Austria

regulation.binding_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 applies alongside the KommAustria-Gesetz/TKG 2021 provisions creating the KI-Servicestelle and the 2026 AVG/VStG amendment on AI in administrative procedures.
regulation.summary: Austria regulates AI through the directly applicable EU AI Act, amended by the Digital Omnibus on AI that entered into force on 24 July 2026 and moved Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 and Annex I embedded systems to 2 August 2028; prohibitions, AI literacy, GPAI duties and Article 50 transparency apply today. Nationally, the Nationalrat adopted an amendment to the Allgemeines Verwaltungsverfahrensgesetz and the Verwaltungsstrafgesetz on 23 September 2026 creating the legal basis for chatbots, fully automated decisions and no-stop procedures in administrative proceedings. National execution lags: no implementing act exists, and the notifying and market surveillance authorities required by Article 70 remain undesignated.

AZE.name: Azerbaijan

regulation.summary: Azerbaijan's primary AI governance instrument remains the AI Strategy 2025–2028 (Presidential Decree No. 530, March 2025), which is non-binding but mandates establishing a dedicated AI legal framework by 2027. The April 2026 Criminal Code amendments (Articles 148-2 and 242-1) introduced the first binding AI-specific criminal penalties—targeting deepfakes and non-consensual AI-generated content—but these are narrow, use-case-specific provisions rather than horizontal AI regulation. No comprehensive binding AI law is in force or in active parliamentary process.

AZE.key_laws: Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the Republic of Azerbaijan for 2025–2028 (Presidential Decree No. 530, 2025), Digital Economy Development Strategy 2026–2029 (Presidential Decree, 2025), Criminal Code amendments introducing Articles 148-2 and 242-1 on illegal AI use (2026), Action Plan for Accelerating Digital Development 2026–2028 (2026)

BHS.name: Bahamas

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding rule is in force, clause 2.8 of the URCA Code of Practice for Content Regulation (Revised 2024); the Electricity Act, 2024 only empowers future AI regulations.
regulation.summary: AI obligations in The Bahamas sit inside sectoral and general instruments: clause 2.8 of URCA's Code of Practice for Content Regulation (Revised 2024) requires licensed broadcasters to maintain internal policies on AI and synthetic media, section 18 of the Electricity Act, 2024 empowers URCA to make AI regulations for the electricity sector on stated principles, and the Data Protection Act, 2025 defines profiling to include artificial intelligence and restricts decisions based solely on automated processing. The Speech from the Throne of May 2026 committed the government to an Artificial Intelligence Governance Act establishing a national AI commission, and the Ministry of Innovation and National Development announced in June 2026 a national AI Committee to draft that legislation, which has not been tabled. Coverage therefore remains narrow and content-specific rather than horizontal.

promotion.note: The Minister of Innovation announced in August 2026 a planned $3m Inter-American Development Bank-funded AI skills programme and a National AI Literacy Initiative, with no sandbox or AI procurement…

BHS.key_laws: Electricity Act (2024), URCA Code of Practice for Content Regulation (Revised 2024, ECS 78/2024), Data Protection Act (2025), Data Protection (Privacy of Personal Information) Act (2003), Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (announced in the Speech from the Throne, 2026, not yet tabled)

BHR.name: Bahrain

regulation.binding_note: The General Policy for the Use of Artificial Intelligence (v1.0, 30 July 2025) is the single AI-specific instrument mandatory for government entities; the draft AI law is not in force.
regulation.summary: Bahrain's standalone 38-article Artificial Intelligence Regulation Law, unanimously approved by the Shura Council in April 2024, was returned by the Cabinet with objections and was still not enacted when the Shura Legislative and Legal Affairs Committee described continued drafting on an EU- and Arab-model basis in June 2026. The instrument that applies today is the Information & eGovernment Authority's General Policy for the Use of Artificial Intelligence (Version 1.0, 30 July 2025), an AI-specific directive limited to government entities, alongside the Personal Data Protection Law (2018) and the Information Technology Crimes Law (2014), which contain no provisions written for AI.

promotion.note: Tamkeen's AI workforce programme toward 50,000 skilled workers by 2030, the iGA AI Talent Program (June 2025) and the Bahrain Polytechnic AI Academy run alongside AI procurement guidelines, but no…

BGD.name: Bangladesh

regulation.binding_note: AI obligations exist only as provisions inside the Cyber Security (Amendment) Act 2026; no standalone AI-specific binding instrument is in force.
regulation.summary: Bangladesh has no AI-specific statute; the Cyber Security (Amendment) Act 2026, passed on 30 June 2026, inserts obligations on removal of harmful and defamatory AI-generated content and platform response timeframes, giving the country one narrow binding AI rule. The National AI Policy 2026-2030 (Draft v2, 9 February 2026) completed public consultation on 8 February 2026 and remains unadopted, while the Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Ministry said on 2 September 2026 that a draft AI law will go to parliament after expert review. Personal Data Protection Ordinance 2025 and National Data Governance Ordinance 2025, gazetted on 9 November 2025, touch AI only incidentally.

promotion.note: The draft policy proposes a regulatory sandbox, a national AI cloud and a University Grants Commission AI research hub, none of which is operational.

BGD.key_laws: Cyber Security (Amendment) Act (2026), Cyber Security Ordinance (2025), Personal Data Protection Ordinance (2025), National Data Governance Ordinance (2025), National AI Policy 2026-2030 (Draft v2, 2026), National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence (2020)

regulation.binding_note: Only general legislation, the Data Protection Act, 2019-29, applies to AI-related processing; no AI-specific binding instrument exists.
regulation.summary: Barbados governs AI through general law only: the Data Protection Act, 2019-29 covers automated processing and profiling and requires data protection impact assessments for decisions based on automated processing, but contains nothing written for AI systems. No AI bill has been laid before Parliament, and the Cybercrime Bill, 2024 debate concerned online speech rather than AI. Government activity in 2026 consisted of ministerial statements, skills programmes and international advocacy rather than legislation.

promotion.note: A 12-week deep tech fellowship on AI, data systems and digital governance ran with the Ministry of Industry, Innovation, Science and Technology; no AI funding scheme, sandbox or procurement rules…

BLR.name: Belarus

regulation.binding_note: Only general instruments reach AI: Law No. 99-Z on Personal Data Protection (2021) and Decree No. 8 on the Development of the Digital Economy (2017) governing the High-Tech Park.
regulation.summary: Belarus has no enacted AI-specific legislation. A national law on AI technologies, drafted by the United Institute of Informatics Problems of the National Academy of Sciences on the basis of the CIS Model Law on Artificial Intelligence Technologies and worked on by a 42-member cross-ministerial group, remains at the preparatory stage; on 6 September 2026 the Council of the Republic's expert advisory council confirmed that legislative work continues without a bill before parliament. The only AI-specific binding text in preparation is a July 2026 draft amendment to Law No. 99-Z on Personal Data Protection requiring notification and consent where AI is used for legally significant decisions.

promotion.note: The State Program "Digital Belarus" 2026–2030 (Resolution No. 793 of 30 December 2025) funds 21 measures including a state digital platform "Artificial Intelligence"; no AI regulatory sandbox…

BEL.name: Belgium

regulation.binding_note: Two AI-specific binding instruments apply: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, and the Royal Decree of 20 July 2026 IPI code of ethics with its AI chapter.
regulation.summary: Belgium is governed by the directly applicable EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689): prohibited practices and AI-literacy duties since 2 February 2025, general-purpose AI model and penalty provisions since 2 August 2025, and Article 50 transparency duties since 2 August 2026, while Annex III high-risk obligations now fall on 2 December 2027 under Digital Omnibus Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. No national AI statute has been enacted; BIPT's role rests on the Government Declaration of 31 January 2025 and the 2025-2029 Federal Government Agreement rather than legislation. A Royal Decree of 20 July 2026 approving the Professional Institute of Real Estate Agents code of ethics, in force 1 October 2026, adds a binding AI chapter for one profession.

promotion.note: TRAIL (€32M), Flemish AI research and AI Academie programmes and EuroHPC participation are funded, while BIPT guidance places an operational AI regulatory sandbox only at 2 August 2027.

BLZ.name: Belize

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument is in force: Practice Direction No. 18 of 2025 of the Senior Courts of Belize.
regulation.summary: Belize has no AI statute and no national AI strategy; the Data Protection Act 2021, Digital Government Act 2022 and Telecommunications Act (Cap. 229) contain no AI-specific provisions. The single binding AI-specific instrument is Practice Direction No. 18 of 2025, Ethical Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Court Proceedings, in force in the Senior Courts since 12 August 2025, which sets disclosure and verification duties for judges, attorneys and court staff. Economy-wide AI activity remains confined to policy documents such as the Global Digital Services Investment Policy and Strategy (2025) and the National Digital Infrastructure Plan (2025), which impose no obligations.

promotion.note: IDB-supported digital programmes including the National Digital Infrastructure Plan (2025) contain no AI-specific funding line, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rule.

BEN.name: Benin

regulation.binding_note: Only general law applies to AI: the Code du Numérique and Loi No. 2009-09 enforced by the Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel.
regulation.summary: Benin regulates AI through a strategy rather than law: the SNIAM 2023-2027, approved by the Council of Ministers on 18 January 2023, sets objectives and four programmes but imposes no obligations. Binding rules touching AI come only from general instruments, the Code du Numérique (Loi No. 2017-20 of 2018, amended by Loi No. 2020-35 of 2021) and Loi No. 2009-09 on personal data, neither of which contains provisions written for AI systems. Creation in May 2026 of a Ministry of Digital Transformation and Innovation explicitly charged with the national AI strategy did not add any binding instrument.

promotion.note: Capacity and ecosystem programmes exist (Sèmè City, École d'Été en Intelligence Artificielle, hackathons and startup financing under SNIAM), with no AI regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules.

BEN.key_laws: Stratégie Nationale d'Intelligence Artificielle et des Mégadonnées (SNIAM) 2023-2027, Code du Numérique (Loi No. 2017-20 of 2018, amended by Loi No. 2020-35 of 2021), Loi No. 2009-09 of 2009 on Protection of Personally Identifiable Information

BTN.name: Bhutan

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument exists, and GovTech states Bhutan has no data protection regulation that could be applied to AI.
regulation.summary: Bhutan governs AI through soft instruments: the National AI Strategy (NAIS) 2025, the Guideline for Generative Artificial Intelligence Usage in the Civil Service 2024 issued by the Royal Civil Service Commission with GovTech, and the Bhutan AI Readiness Assessment (AIRA) 2024. The National Assembly's June 2025 motion called for a regulatory framework, but no AI bill has reached the legislature and Bhutan also lacks a general data protection statute. Coverage of AI obligations extends only to civil servants, on a non-binding basis.

promotion.note: GovTech runs the AI Startup Program and earlier the AI Lab Program with Omdena, DHI and Thimphu TechPark; no regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules exist.

BOL.name: Bolivia

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument exists; Bolivia also lacks a comprehensive data protection law that regulators could apply to AI.
regulation.summary: Bolivia has no enacted AI law. The only AI-specific legislative instrument, Proyecto de Ley 178/2024-2025 on the promotion, management and use of artificial intelligence, was passed by the Senate on 22 October 2025 with 31 articles creating an AI regulatory authority, prohibited practices and fines, and awaits treatment in the Chamber of Deputies. Regional commitments under the Santiago Declaration (2023) and Cartagena Declaration (2024) remain non-binding.

promotion.note: The Ministry of Planning launched the state-built BolivIA model in August 2026, but no AI funding scheme, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules exist.

BIH.name: Bosnia and Herz.

regulation.binding_note: Only general law applies to AI, principally the Law on Personal Data Protection (Official Gazette of BiH 12/25) enforced by the Personal Data Protection Agency.
regulation.summary: There is no dedicated AI law, no state-level AI strategy and no binding AI-specific rule in force or before the Parliamentary Assembly. The only national commitment to binding AI obligations is the signature of the Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law on 9 December 2025, which has not been ratified; AI reaches domestic law only through the automated decision-making provisions of the Law on Personal Data Protection (Official Gazette of BiH 12/25).

promotion.note: No state funding program, AI procurement rule or regulatory sandbox exists; AI capacity work is donor-financed through UNDP projects.

BIH.key_laws: Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (CETS No. 225, signed 9 December 2025, not ratified), Law on Personal Data Protection of Bosnia and Herzegovina (2025, Official Gazette of BiH 12/25), Roadmap for Artificial Intelligence of the Parliamentary Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina (2026), Development Strategy of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina 2021-2027 (entity-level, mentions artificial intelligence)

BWA.name: Botswana

regulation.binding_note: Only general law applies, principally the Data Protection Act, 2024 whose automated-processing and profiling duties bind data controllers.
regulation.summary: Botswana has no AI-specific legislation in force or before Parliament; the first National Artificial Intelligence Policy, informed by the UNESCO Readiness Assessment Methodology completed in 2024-2025, is still at drafting stage. AI is reached only incidentally by general digital law: the Data Protection Act, 2024 (Act No. 18 of 2024, effective 14 January 2025) regulates solely automated decision-making and profiling and requires impact assessments for automated processing, while the Digital Services Act, 2025 and Cybersecurity Act, 2025 carry no AI provisions.

promotion.note: AI is named among the FY2025/26 national research and development priorities, with no dedicated AI fund, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rule established.

BRA.name: Brazil

regulation.binding_note: Lei 15.123/2025 and TSE Resolution 23.755/2026 bind today, joined by CFM Resolution 2.454/2026 and Portaria MGI 3.485/2026; the cross-sector PL 2338/2023 is unenacted.
regulation.summary: Brazil regulates AI through a patchwork of sector-specific binding instruments — TSE Resolution 23.755 of 2 March 2026 on synthetic content in electoral propaganda, CFM Resolution 2.454/2026 on AI in medicine, Portaria MGI 3.485 of 24 April 2026 on AI governance in the federal administration, and Lei 15.123/2025 criminalising AI-assisted violence against women — alongside general law (LGPD Law 13.709/2018, Marco Civil Law 12.965/2014, ECA Digital Law 15.211/2025 in force since 17 March 2026). The horizontal AI Legal Framework, PL 2338/2023, was approved by the Senate on 10 December 2024 but remains before the Chamber of Deputies special committee, with the rapporteur confirming on 24 August 2026 that the vote would follow the October 2026 elections. Obligations therefore apply only in defined domains, not economy-wide.

promotion.note: PBIA 2024–2028 funding and Lei 15.504/2026 data-centre tax incentives (sanctioned 16 September 2026) run alongside ANPD's AI sandbox, whose testing phase runs to December 2026; no government-wide AI…

BRN.name: Brunei

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: the Personal Data Protection Order 2025, administered by AITI, with substantive provisions effective 1 January 2026.
regulation.summary: Brunei regulates AI through voluntary means: the Guide on Artificial Intelligence Governance and Ethics for Brunei Darussalam, issued by AITI in April 2025 and reissued as a second edition in 2026, carries no legal force. The binding law reaching AI is general: the Personal Data Protection Order 2025, whose substantive provisions commenced on 1 January 2026 and which AITI administers. No AI-specific binding instrument exists or is before the legislature.

promotion.note: Digital Brunei 2030 announces SME pilot projects and AI adoption indicators; no AI-specific funding scheme, procurement rule or AI regulatory sandbox operates.

BGR.name: Bulgaria

regulation.binding_note: The EU AI Act is the single AI-specific binding instrument applying in Bulgaria; no national AI statute or secondary act has been adopted.
regulation.summary: Bulgaria's binding AI framework is the directly applicable EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), whose prohibitions, AI-literacy, general-purpose AI and transparency duties apply, while high-risk obligations were pushed to 2 December 2027 by the 2026 Digital Omnibus amendment. No national supplementary law is in force: a government bill was announced as nearing public consultation in September 2026 and an opposition Act on the Use and Development of Artificial Intelligence (bill 52-654-01-151) was tabled in the National Assembly on 24 September 2026 after an earlier version was rejected in committee.

promotion.note: State-backed research capacity (INSAIT, EuroHPC Discoverer) exists while the proposed AI regulatory sandbox with a EUR 213,520 budget was ranked low priority by the Ministry of Finance in October…

BFA.name: Burkina Faso

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: Loi n°001-2021/AN on personal data protection and the 2024 loi portant sécurité des systèmes d'information.
regulation.summary: Burkina Faso has no dedicated AI law and none before the Assemblée législative du peuple; the only binding provision written for AI is Article 19 of Loi n°001-2021/AN portant protection des données à caractère personnel, which obliges controllers to disclose the criteria and data underlying AI-based processing. The Feuille de route nationale sur l'intelligence artificielle 2026-2030, validated on 17 June 2026 under the Plan RELANCE 2026-2030 and the 'IA pour tous' programme, is a strategy without binding force, and deputies were given an AI briefing on 15 July 2026 to prepare future digital legislation.

promotion.note: The 'IA pour tous' programme and roadmap priorities in health, agriculture and education are announced without disbursed funding, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules.

BDI.name: Burundi

regulation.binding_note: Only general instruments apply, namely Loi n°1/03 du 10 mars 2026 on personal data protection and Loi n°1/10 du 16 mars 2022 on cybercrime.
regulation.summary: Burundi has no binding AI legislation; its only AI-specific instrument is the Stratégie Nationale de l'Intelligence Artificielle 2026-2030, validated in Bujumbura on 21-22 April 2026 by the Ministry of Finance, Budget and Digital Economy with UNDP support, which is a six-pillar non-binding roadmap promising later regulatory and ethical frameworks. General law reaches AI indirectly through Loi n°1/03 of 10 March 2026 on personal data protection and Loi n°1/10 of 16 March 2022 on cybercrime, neither of which regulates AI systems as such.

promotion.note: The strategy announces pilot projects in health and agriculture while financing and partnerships remain under negotiation, as presented at the KOAFEC ministerial in Seoul in September 2026.

KHM.name: Cambodia

regulation.binding_note: Only general law touches AI: Sub-Decree 110 (2017) on the ICT Licensing Regime and the Law on Anti-Technology Fraud (2026).
regulation.summary: Cambodia governs AI through general instruments only: Sub-Decree 110 (2017) on the ICT Licensing Regime covers the supply side of AI, and the Law on Anti-Technology Fraud passed on 3 April 2026 criminalises technology-enabled fraud without AI-specific provisions. The Draft National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025-2030, the Draft MPTC AI Promotion Strategy and the Draft Law on Personal Data Protection are all still in consultation, and the strategy itself commits to a light-touch, step-by-step approach rather than a comprehensive AI law.

promotion.note: The draft strategy sets investment and adoption targets and government AI tools (Sarika, TranslateKH, ai.gov.kh) are deployed, with no AI funding programme, sandbox or AI procurement rule established.

CMR.name: Cameroon

regulation.binding_note: The only binding instrument reaching AI is general law: Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on personal data protection.
regulation.summary: Cameroon has no binding AI-specific legislation and no AI bill before the legislature. The National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (SNIA), unveiled in July 2025 by the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications, is a non-binding roadmap whose first pillar proposes a Cameroonian AI Authority, a Presidential Council on AI and a future framework law. Law No. 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on personal data protection became fully applicable on 24 June 2026 after its eighteen-month compliance period, but it is a general-purpose instrument.

promotion.note: SNIA targets such as five AI centres of excellence and regional edge-computing nodes are announced without disbursed funding, a sandbox or AI procurement rules.

CAN.name: Canada

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding federal instrument is in force, the Treasury Board Directive on Automated Decision-Making (2019, updated 24 June 2025).
regulation.summary: Canada has no binding federal AI statute: AIDA died with Bill C-27 in January 2025 and the June 2026 national strategy AI for All chose targeted legislation over a standalone AI act. Binding federal AI rules exist only inside government through the Treasury Board Directive on Automated Decision-Making, whose 2025 version and Algorithmic Impact Assessment apply to federal automated decision systems including generative AI. Bill C-34, the Safe Social Media Act, which would impose duties on AI chatbot services, and Bill C-36, which adds automated-decision transparency rights, were tabled in June 2026 and remain before the House of Commons.

promotion.note: AI for All (4 June 2026) adds a CA$500M Canadian Tech Growth Fund, CA$50M for CAISI and CA$200M+ for national AI institutes, with no operating federal AI regulatory sandbox.

CPV.name: Cape Verde

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: the personal data protection regime (Lei n.º 121/IX/2021), the cybercrime law and the electronic commerce law.
regulation.summary: Cabo Verde has no AI-specific legislation and none in the legislative process; AI is addressed only through strategy documents, notably the Agenda Digital de Cabo Verde 2035 approved by Resolução n.º 72/2026 and the National Data Strategy developed with World Bank support. General instruments — the personal data protection law as amended by Lei n.º 121/IX/2021, the cybercrime law and the electronic commerce law — reach AI uses without containing any AI-written provision, and the Comissão Nacional de Proteção de Dados has publicly framed AI as a data-governance question rather than applying dedicated rules.

promotion.note: A Centro de Excelência Digital e de Inteligência Artificial is announced in the government's digital economy programme but not yet established, and no AI sandbox or procurement rule exists.

CAF.name: Central African Rep.

regulation.binding_note: Loi n° 24-001 (2024) on personal data protection is the only binding instrument reaching automated data processing; no AI-specific instrument exists.
regulation.summary: The Central African Republic has no AI-specific legislation, no draft AI bill and no national AI strategy. The only binding text reaching algorithmic activity is Loi n° 24-001 (2024) on personal data protection, which regulates processing of personal data generally and for which no supervisory authority has been publicly identified. Ongoing conflict and limited state capacity keep AI rulemaking absent from the legislative agenda.

promotion.note: A partnership with an Indian provider to create an AI centre of excellence was announced in 2025 without disbursed funding, sandbox or AI procurement rules.

TCD.name: Chad

regulation.binding_note: The only binding rules reaching AI are the general Loi n°007/PR/2015 on personal data protection and Loi n°009/PR/2015 on cybersecurity, neither written for AI.
regulation.summary: Chad has no AI-specific legislation or regulatory framework. AI activity falls only under general digital law — Loi n°007/PR/2015 on personal data protection and Loi n°009/PR/2015 on cybersecurity and cybercrime, both administered by the Agence Nationale de Sécurité Informatique et de Certification Électronique (ANSICE) — and the draft Code du numérique in preparation since December 2025 adds no AI-specific obligations. The only AI-specific state act is Décret n°2690/PR/PM/MTENDA/2025 of 21 October 2025, which reorganised the Ministry of Telecommunications, Digital Economy and Digitalisation of the Administration and created a Direction générale de l'Intelligence Artificielle without conferring regulatory powers.

promotion.note: An AI skills programme to train 2,000 young people was announced with ADETIC and partners; no national AI fund, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules exist.

CHL.name: Chile

regulation.binding_note: Only general law applies to AI: Law 21.663 on cybersecurity in force, and Law 21.719 on data protection not effective until 1 December 2026.
regulation.summary: No AI-specific statute binds in Chile: the government AI bill (Boletín 16821-19) is in its second constitutional stage before the Senate Future Challenges Committee, and the Executive announced in May 2026 and reiterated in October 2026 a total substitutive indication that would drop the EU-style risk tiers for an innovation-oriented framework. Binding rules reaching AI are general: Law 21.663 on cybersecurity (in force since 2025) and Law 21.719 on personal data protection, which takes effect 1 December 2026 and whose postponement to 2027 is sought by Boletín 18.623-07.

promotion.note: Publicly funded CENIA launched Latam-GPT in February 2026 and MinCiencia committed around 100 state AI pilots for 2026-2030; no AI regulatory sandbox or binding AI procurement rules operate.

CHN.name: China

Obligations such as algorithm filing, security assessment and content labeling apply today across online services, finance, education and healthcare platforms, but the generative AI rules exempt non-public-facing systems and the State Council's 2026 Legislative Work Plan still lists comprehensive AI legislation as pending.

promotion.note: The AI Plus Action Plan (August 2025), state AI investment funds and innovation pilot zones are funded and sectoral sandboxes exist for autonomous driving, with no general AI-specific public…

The binding rules that exist are AI provisions inserted into general law—Ley 2502 de 2025 on AI-assisted identity impersonation and SIC External Circular No. 2 of 2024 on personal data in AI systems—while CONPES 4144 de 2025 remains a non-binding policy roadmap.

COM.name: Comoros

promotion.note: No AI funding scheme, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rule exists; Comores Numérique 2028 funds connectivity and e-government only.

COG.name: Congo

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument is in force; AI is reached through Loi n° 29-2019 on personal data protection and telecoms rules under Loi n° 11-2009.

promotion.note: Delivered programs include MICITT-UNESCO and MICITT-Cisco AI training for public servants and the planned National AI Centre of Excellence; no regulatory sandbox operates and no AI procurement rules…

HRV.name: Croatia

regulation.binding_note: The AI Act as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 is the only AI-specific binding instrument applicable in Croatia; no national AI statute is in force.
regulation.summary: Croatia's binding AI framework is the directly applicable EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), whose prohibitions, general-purpose AI duties and Article 50 transparency obligations apply, while Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), in force since 27 July 2026, moved high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028. promotion.note: Funding runs through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan and EuroHPC-cofunded Supek and Bura supercomputers, with no AI regulatory sandbox established by the 2 August 2026 deadline.

regulation.binding_note: Only general instruments apply: Ley 149/2022 on personal data protection, Resolución 58/2022 of MINCOM and Decreto-Ley 35/2021 on telecommunications.
regulation.summary: Cuba governs AI through the Estrategia para el Desarrollo y Uso de la Inteligencia Artificial, approved in May 2024 as part of the Política para la Transformación Digital y Agenda Digital, a policy document without binding force. promotion.note: The Consorcio de Inteligencia Artificial de Cuba (November 2025) pools 22 institutions under the Parque Científico Tecnológico de La Habana, with no dedicated AI fund, sandbox or AI procurement rules.

CYP.name: Cyprus

regulation.summary: Cyprus is governed by the directly applicable EU AI Act, whose prohibitions, AI literacy duty, general-purpose AI rules and Article 50 transparency obligations bind today, while high-risk system obligations were pushed back to December 2027 and August 2028 by the Digital Omnibus on AI. regulation.summary: Czechia regulates AI chiefly through the directly applicable EU AI Act, whose prohibitions, AI literacy, general-purpose AI and Article 50 transparency duties apply, while Annex III high-risk obligations were postponed to 2 December 2027 by the Digital Omnibus Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. CIV.name: Côte d'Ivoire

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: Loi 2013-450 on personal data protection, supervised by ARTCI, with no AI-specific binding instrument.
regulation.summary: Côte d'Ivoire has no binding AI-specific legislation. Governance rests on the Stratégie Nationale de l'Intelligence Artificielle (SNIA 2030), launched 13 March 2025, the Stratégie Nationale de Gouvernance des Données (SNGD 2030, April 2025) and the digital roadmap to 2035 presented on 1 June 2026, all non-binding strategic documents, while general instruments such as Loi 2013-450 on personal data protection touch AI only incidentally. Parliament opened its October 2026 session with AI on the agenda for member training rather than a bill.

promotion.note: More than 1,000 billion FCFA is budgeted for AI and data under SNIA 2030 for 2025-2030, with no disbursed AI programme, sandbox or AI procurement rule.

COD.name: Dem. Rep. Congo

regulation.binding_note: Only general law applies to AI: the Code du numérique's data-protection, cybersecurity and digital-offence provisions, with no AI-specific binding instrument.
regulation.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has no AI-specific legislation or bill; AI reaches the statute book only through the Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 du 13 mars 2023 portant Code du numérique, which covers personal data, cybersecurity and digital services and mentions artificial intelligence among the ethics matters a national digital body must watch over. Policy direction now rests on the Stratégie nationale de l'intelligence artificielle (SNIA) and the Politique sectorielle de l'économie numérique (PSEN), both presented and validated by the government in Kinshasa on 4 August 2026, which carry no binding force. UNESCO's Readiness Assessment Methodology report for the country records the absence of a dedicated AI legal framework, coordination organ or national ethics commission.

promotion.note: The Plan national du numérique 2026-2030 announces about USD 1.5 billion and a Congolese AI academy, with no disbursed AI programme, sandbox or AI procurement rules.

COD.key_laws: Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 du 13 mars 2023 portant Code du numérique, Stratégie nationale de l'intelligence artificielle (2026), Politique sectorielle de l'économie numérique (2026), Plan national du numérique 2026-2030 (2026), Loi n° 20/017 du 25 novembre 2020 relative aux télécommunications et aux technologies de l'information et de la communication

DNK.name: Denmark

regulation.binding_note: Two AI-specific binding instruments apply: the EU AI Act and Lov nr. 467 af 14. maj 2025; the Copyright Act deepfake amendment remains pending.
regulation.summary: Denmark applies the EU AI Act directly, supplemented by Law No. 467 of 14 May 2025 (Act on Supplementary Provisions to the Regulation on Artificial Intelligence), in force from 2 August 2025, which designates Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, Datatilsynet and Domstolsstyrelsen as national competent authorities and sets national fine powers. Prohibited-practice rules have applied since 2 February 2025, general-purpose AI rules since 2 August 2025 and most remaining provisions since 2 August 2026, while Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI) pushed Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 and Annex I to 2 August 2028. A bill amending the Copyright Act to protect against realistic digitally generated imitations of personal characteristics follows the June 2025 cross-party agreement and has not entered into force.

promotion.note: The Datatilsynet-Digitaliseringsstyrelsen AI regulatory sandbox published second-round reports on 1 July 2026 alongside DKK 740 million of digitalisation funding for 2024-2027, with no AI-specific…

DJI.name: Djibouti

regulation.binding_note: Binding instruments reaching AI are general: Code du numérique (2023, data protection provisions 2025) and Loi n°195/AN/25/9ème L on the Autorité Nationale de Cybersécurité.
regulation.summary: Djibouti governs AI through general digital law rather than AI-specific rules: the Code du numérique, in force since 2023 and extended in June 2025 with a 156-article personal data regime, plus Loi n°195/AN/25/9ème L creating the Autorité Nationale de Cybersécurité. The first Stratégie Nationale d'Intelligence Artificielle (SNIA) 2026-2030 was presented at the national AI forum on 3 September 2026 as a non-binding roadmap, and the UNESCO readiness assessment accompanying it places the country at an "emerging" stage with regulation as the weakest area.

promotion.note: The Prix Innovation IA Djibouti 2026 prototyping competition ran at the September 2026 forum; no AI funding line, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rule exists.

DMA.name: Dominica

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument is in force, and Dominica lacks even a general data protection act applicable to automated processing.
regulation.summary: Dominica has no dedicated AI legislation, no binding AI rules and no national AI strategy; the September 2026 Cullen International review of the Caribbean lists only Cuba and the Dominican Republic as having adopted national AI strategies. The only adjacent national instrument is the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2022-2026, which sets digital-government and connectivity goals rather than AI obligations, and the country has not enacted comprehensive data protection legislation that regulators could apply to AI.

promotion.note: No national AI funding programme, AI procurement rule or regulatory sandbox exists; AI activity reaching Dominica is regional, such as the Future Caribbean AI Buildathon.

DMA.key_laws: Dominica National Digital Transformation Strategy 2022-2026 (not AI-specific)

DOM.name: Dominican Republic

regulation.binding_note: Decreto 498-23 (October 2023) is the single AI-specific binding instrument, imposing coordination and budgeting duties on executive bodies for AI projects.
regulation.summary: The only binding AI rules are the articles of the new Penal Code (Ley 74-25), effective 3 August 2026, that criminalise the use of artificial intelligence to fabricate and disseminate false or intimate content. Governance otherwise rests on Decreto 498-23, which approved the Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial (ENIA) and its action plan to 31 December 2030 and obliges executive entities to coordinate AI projects with the Gabinete de Innovación y Desarrollo Digital. Two Senate AI bills were merged into a single text in committee on 15 September 2026 and no AI statute has been enacted.

promotion.note: Programmes comprise the CEIA-RD AI centre built with NVIDIA, whose first phase opens in November 2026, and MAP's 2,000 generative-AI scholarships for public servants; no AI regulatory sandbox…

TLS.name: East Timor

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument exists, and no regulator has applied general law to AI systems.
regulation.summary: Timor-Leste has no AI-specific legislation, and the UNESCO Readiness Assessment Methodology country report completed in 2025 with the Ministry of Transport and Communications confirms the absence of AI provisions in existing ICT and data-privacy law. Governance activity is confined to the Timor Digital 2032 national digital strategy, which is being revised to incorporate AI, and to foundational connectivity and cybersecurity work. Constitutional data-protection rights and general telecommunications and electronic-commerce rules apply without any provision written for AI.

promotion.note: No AI funding programme, AI procurement rule or regulatory sandbox exists; investment is directed to submarine cable and fibre infrastructure.

TLS.key_laws: Timor Digital 2032 National Digital Strategy (2023-2032), UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment Methodology country report for Timor-Leste (2025)

ECU.name: Ecuador

regulation.binding_note: One cross-sector AI-specific binding instrument is in force, Resolución SPDP-SPD-2026-0009-R as reformed, complemented by SPDP-SPD-2026-0007-R governing AI in the authority's own administrative…
regulation.summary: Ecuador regulates AI through subordinate rules of the data protection authority: the Norma General para la Garantía del Derecho de Protección de Datos Personales en el Uso de Sistemas de Inteligencia Artificial (Resolución SPDP-SPD-2026-0009-R), reformed in September 2026, which imposes risk management, impact assessment, transparency and security duties on anyone using AI to process personal data, alongside the biometric-data norm that bans mass facial recognition. No statutory AI law exists: the Asamblea Nacional archived the Proyecto de Ley Orgánica de Regulación y Promoción de la Inteligencia Artificial in September 2026, and the Proyecto de Ley Orgánica para el Desarrollo, Uso Ético y Gobernanza de la Inteligencia Artificial is before the Comisión de Educación.

promotion.note: The 2025-2029 AI strategy was launched in March 2026 without a centralised budget, and no regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules operate.

EGY.name: Egypt

regulation.binding_note: Binding coverage comes only from general law, chiefly Personal Data Protection Law No. 151/2020 and its Executive Regulations No. 816/2025, with no AI-specific binding instrument.
regulation.summary: Egypt governs AI through dedicated non-binding instruments: the Egyptian Charter for Responsible AI (2023), the National AI Strategy Second Edition (2025-2030), and the March 2026 suite comprising the Guide to Egypt's National AI Governance Framework (edition 2.0), the National Guidelines for Trustworthy and Responsible AI (edition 2.0) and the National Generative AI Guidelines, which set a four-tier risk classification and compliance pathways without legal force. The only binding instruments reaching AI are general: Personal Data Protection Law No. 151/2020 with Executive Regulations No. 816/2025 (in force 2 November 2025, compliance deadline 1 November 2026), the Fintech Law No. 5 of 2022, and the cybercrime amendments passed in February 2026, which parliament deliberately kept technology-neutral. The Draft Artificial Intelligence Law has not reached enactment.

promotion.note: Applied Innovation Center, Egyptian AI Institute and 'Our Future is Digital' training operate, while the national AI sandbox agreed with UNDP in July 2026 is not yet operating and no AI procurement…

SLV.name: El Salvador

regulation.binding_note: Decreto 234 (2025), Decreto 363 (2025) and Resolución ANIA 0001/2025 are in force, and a special-provisions decree for national AI and robotics projects was approved on 23 September 2026.
regulation.summary: El Salvador governs AI through a dedicated statute, the Ley de Fomento a Inteligencia Artificial y Tecnologías (Decreto Legislativo 234 of 26 February 2025), reformed by Decreto 363 (2025), and operative secondary rules in ANIA Resolución 0001/2025, applicable since 2 September 2025, which define 'consequential decisions' and require registration in six domains spanning health, credit and insurance, biometrics, public powers, employment and education. Duties also include disclosure that a decision was AI-driven and a route to contest it before a human reviewer. Obligations apply across sectors today, but there is no penalty regime and compliance rests on self-certification and evidence requests.

promotion.note: The September 2026 decree creates a direct-contracting procurement regime for national AI projects and Decreto 234 provides sandbox safeguards, with no evidence of an operating regulatory sandbox.

GNQ.name: Equatorial Guinea

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument exists, and Ley 1/2016 has not been applied to AI because its governing body was never established.
regulation.summary: Equatorial Guinea has no AI-specific law in force and no published national AI strategy. The Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Artificial Intelligence Systems has run drafting sessions in Malabo on terms of reference for a future AI law, including a proposed national AI and data authority, but no text has been published, tabled or enacted. The nearest binding instrument, Ley 1/2016 de Protección de Datos de Carácter Personal, says nothing about AI and its supervisory body remains unappointed.

promotion.note: No AI funding programme, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rule has been established.

regulation.binding_note: No binding AI instrument exists, and no general law such as data protection has been enacted or applied to AI.
regulation.summary: Eritrea has no AI-specific legislation, no draft AI bill and no AI provision inside general law. The only relevant legal anchors are the Communications Proclamation No. 102/1998, administered by the Ministry of Transport and Communications, and the privacy guarantee of the 1997 Constitution, which has never entered into force; neither mentions artificial intelligence. There is also no data protection law or authority to which AI governance could attach.

promotion.note: No AI funding scheme, procurement rule or regulatory sandbox exists; the state monopoly EriTel operates one of the world's least connected networks.

EST.name: Estonia

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument applies, the EU AI Act; Estonia added no national AI-specific binding act, only GDPR and the Personal Data Protection Act as general law.
regulation.summary: Estonia enacted no standalone national AI statute and relies on the directly applicable EU AI Act, whose prohibitions, AI literacy duty, GPAI rules and Article 50 transparency obligations apply while Annex III high-risk duties were postponed to 2 December 2027 by the Digital Omnibus on AI, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. National implementation consists of authority designations published on kratid.ee and TTJA guidance, with the amendment to the General Part of the Economic Activities Code Act and the State Fees Act creating the AI regulatory sandbox and the penalty regime still in the legislative pipeline. Domestic soft-law instruments, the AI and Data Action Plan (Kratt) 2024–2026 and the Data and AI White Paper 2024–2030, carry no binding force.

promotion.note: Eesti.ai, the AI Leap (TI-hüpe) education programme and Kratt-plan funding operate, while the statutory basis for the national AI regulatory sandbox remained in the draft MsÜS and State Fees Act…

ETH.name: Ethiopia

regulation.binding_note: Regulation No. 510/2022 is the single AI-specific binding instrument in force; Proclamation No. 1321/2024 is general data law.
regulation.summary: Ethiopia governs AI through the non-binding National Artificial Intelligence Policy adopted by the Council of Ministers in June 2024, supported by Artificial Intelligence Institute Establishment Council of Ministers Regulation No. 510/2022, which creates the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute and gives it evaluation and certification functions over imported AI systems. Binding obligations on AI developers and deployers come only from general law, chiefly the Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024, and the draft National Data Governance Proclamation referred to the House of Peoples' Representatives on 28 September 2026 regulates data use for AI rather than AI systems. No cross-sector AI statute has been tabled.

promotion.note: EAII runs an AI Startup Center with a 2026 Cohort II incubation programme and the EthiopiAI grant scheme funds responsible AI projects.

FJI.name: Fiji

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: Online Safety Act 2018 and Cybercrime Act 2021, with no dedicated personal data protection statute yet enacted.
regulation.summary: Fiji has no binding AI-specific legislation; AI governance commitments sit in the Cabinet-approved National Digital Strategy 2025-2030, a non-binding planning document, alongside a 2024 ministerial announcement of a framework to protect users from AI threats. Oversight of AI-related harms falls back on the Online Safety Act 2018 and the Cybercrime Act 2021, which contain no AI-written provisions, and the Ministry of Education's AI policy for schools was still at consultation stage in September 2026.

promotion.note: The AI Hub launched in 2024 with Australia Fiji Business Council support and further Ministry of Trade AI hubs operate, while the Reserve Bank of Fiji's FinTech Regulatory Sandbox is not AI-specific.

FJI.key_laws: National Digital Strategy 2025-2030, Online Safety Act (2018), Cybercrime Act (2021), National Privacy and Personal Data Protection Policy (2025), Pacific Digital and Artificial Intelligence Technology Principles (2026)

FIN.name: Finland

regulation.binding_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Act 1377/2025 and the AI-specific amendments to the Market Surveillance of Products Act are in force, with high-risk obligations not yet applicable.
regulation.summary: Finland is governed by the directly applicable EU AI Act, supplemented by the national Act on the Supervision of Certain Artificial Intelligence Systems (1377/2025) and amendments to market surveillance, Financial Supervisory Authority and Energy Authority legislation in force since 1 January 2026. Prohibited-practice, general-purpose AI and Article 50 transparency obligations bind actors today, with Traficom supervising transparency since 2 August 2026, while high-risk system duties were postponed to 2 December 2027 by the Digital Omnibus on AI. The second national implementing act, covering the regulatory sandbox and the register of high-risk AI used in critical infrastructure, remains in preparation.

promotion.note: Business Finland AI funding, the LUMI AI ecosystem, Elements of AI and participation in the EU ALT-EDIC consortium operate, while the national AI regulatory sandbox awaits legislation with the EU…

FRA.name: France

regulation.binding_note: The AI Act plus the deepfake offences of loi n°2024-449 (SREN), the algorithmic video-surveillance regime of loi n°2023-380 and Article L.4001-3 of the health code are AI-specific and in force.
regulation.summary: France applies the EU AI Act directly: prohibitions and AI literacy since 2 February 2025, GPAI obligations since 2 August 2025 and Article 50 transparency since 2 August 2026, with high-risk obligations postponed to 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 by the Digital Omnibus Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. Domestic AI-specific rules exist for deepfakes (loi SREN of 21 May 2024), algorithmic video surveillance (loi of 19 May 2023, experiment extended to 1 March 2027) and patient information on medical AI (Article L.4001-3 of the Code de la santé publique). The national designation of competent authorities and penalty rules remains in the DDADUE bill before the Assemblée nationale, leaving implementation incomplete.

promotion.note: France 2030 funds the national AI strategy with roughly €2.2 billion and Bpifrance programmes, while no AI Act Article 57 national regulatory sandbox is operating and no binding AI procurement rules…

GAB.name: Gabon

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument is in force, Ordonnance n°0011/PR/2026, complemented by the AI definitions inserted into the data protection law by Loi n°025/2023.
regulation.summary: Gabon's binding AI rules sit inside Ordonnance n°0011/PR/2026 du 26 février 2026 on the use of social networks via digital platforms, which defines AI systems and AI-generated content, prohibits non-consensual deepfakes and false-attribution deepfakes, imposes labelling of synthetic content and a 24-hour takedown right, and gives the Haute Autorité de la Communication audit powers over detection systems. Loi n°025/2023 du 12 juillet 2023 amending the personal data protection law adds AI definitions and rules on automated decision-making and profiling. Coverage is confined to online content and personal data, and operators have a twelve-month period to come into conformity.;

promotion.note: A decree of 22 May 2026 creates a startup regulatory framework and label and the Gabonese Innovation Centre operates, but no AI-specific fund, sandbox or AI procurement rule exists.

GMB.name: Gambia

regulation.summary: Gambia has no dedicated AI legislation, strategy, or binding regulatory instrument as of mid-2026. Existing ICT and data protection frameworks do not directly address artificial intelligence, and no AI-specific bills have been introduced into the National Assembly.

GMB.key_laws: Information and Communications Act (2009), Gambia Information and Communications Infrastructure Authority Act

GEO.name: Georgia

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument is in force, the National Bank of Georgia regulation on risk management of data-based statistical, AI and machine-learning models.
regulation.summary: Georgia has no cross-sector AI law and no adopted national AI strategy; the UNESCO Readiness Assessment Methodology country report delivered in February 2026 and the June 2026 UNESCO roadmap article describe the country as at a foundational stage and propose a phased path to regulation. The one binding AI-specific instrument is the National Bank of Georgia Regulation on Managing Risks for Data-based Statistical, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Models, which applies to financial institutions. The Law on Personal Data Protection No. 3144/2023, in force since March 2024, covers profiling and automated decision-making, and the Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence (CETS No. 225), signed in September 2024, is not ratified.

promotion.note: The 2026 State Budget allocates about USD 18.4 million for AI research for 2026-2029 and GITA runs innovation and startup programs touching AI; no AI regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules exist.

DEU.name: Germany

regulation.binding_note: Two AI-specific binding instruments apply nationally, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and KI-MIG, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, with high-risk parts not yet applicable.
regulation.summary: Germany applies the directly binding EU AI Act and executes it nationally through the Gesetz zur Marktüberwachung und Innovationsförderung von künstlicher Intelligenz (KI-MIG), in force since 29 July 2026, which designates competent authorities, sets the national penalty framework and creates an AI regulatory sandbox. promotion.note: Hightech Agenda Deutschland KI funding and AI compute programmes are disbursing, while the statutory KI-Reallabor remains in build-up after the March 2026 simulated-sandbox pilot report.

GHA.name: Ghana

regulation.binding_note: Only general statutes, the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) and Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038), apply to AI deployments.
regulation.summary: Ghana has no binding AI legislation; the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2025-2035, launched by President Mahama on 24 April 2026, is a policy roadmap, while the Emerging Technologies Bill, 2025 (proposing an Emerging Technologies Agency) sits in public consultation and the Data Protection Bill, 2025, which would regulate AI systems, automated decision-making and deepfakes, has not been enacted. Operative rules reaching AI are the general Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) and Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038), applied by the Data Protection Commission and Cyber Security Authority without AI-specific provisions.

promotion.note: Cabinet approved USD 250 million for a national AI Computing Centre in April 2026 plus USD 20 million for strategy implementation; the Bank of Ghana sandbox is not AI-specific.

GRC.name: Greece

regulation.binding_note: Two AI-specific binding instruments are in force: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended and Law 5321/2026, with parts of the former not yet applicable.
regulation.summary: Greece is covered by the directly applicable EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) and has enacted Law 5321/2026 on measures implementing it, published in Government Gazette A' 114 of 20 July 2026, which designates competent authorities, creates complaint and sanction procedures, a public-sector AI registry, an AI Observatory and deepfake transparency duties, and repeals the AI chapter of Law 4961/2022. Prohibited practices, general-purpose AI duties and Article 50 transparency obligations apply today, while the Annex III high-risk regime was deferred to 2 December 2027 and the Annex I regime to 2 August 2028 by the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744). Implementation is advanced on institutions but incomplete on deadlines, standards and the regulatory sandbox.

promotion.note: Pharos AI Factory (EUR 30 million, EuroHPC co-funded) and the DAEDALUS supercomputer (EUR 58.9 million) are funded, while the Law 5321/2026 sandbox is not yet operating.

GRD.name: Grenada

regulation.binding_note: No binding AI instrument exists, and the one general data law, the Data Protection Act, No. 1 of 2023, is not yet in operation.
regulation.summary: Grenada has no AI-specific legislation, draft bill or regulatory proposal, and the September 2026 Caribbean regulatory review confirms no Caribbean state covered, including Grenada, has adopted an AI-specific framework. The closest adjacent instrument, the Data Protection Act, No. 1 of 2023, was assented to on 9 May 2023 but has not been brought into force and contains no provision written for AI. Government AI activity is confined to adoption of tools in Parliament and the public service rather than regulation.

promotion.note: Parliament announced procurement of AI tools for members from 2025 and the Division of ICT lists AI-powered government tools among priorities, with no funding program, sandbox or AI procurement rules.

GRD.key_laws: Data Protection Act, No. 1 of 2023 (assented 9 May 2023, not yet in force)

GTM.name: Guatemala

regulation.binding_note: No binding AI instrument exists and no general law has been formally applied to AI systems by a Guatemalan regulator.
regulation.summary: Guatemala has no AI-specific law in force and relies on general frameworks such as the Law on Access to Public Information, Decree 57-2008. Two tracks are open in Congress: Iniciativa 6657 (2025), which would criminalise malicious AI-generated content, and competing personal data protection bills (Iniciativas 6105, 6572 and 6626), none of which has been reported out of committee. A government AI strategy led by the Secretaría Nacional de Ciencia y Tecnología is due to be finalised at the end of 2026, with a multisectoral national strategy scheduled for the first quarter of 2027.

promotion.note: UNDP's AI Sprint and AI for Local Development Challenge operate with external funding; no national AI fund, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rule exists.

GTM.key_laws: Law on Access to Public Information, Decree 57-2008 (incidentally touches personal data); Iniciativa 6657, bill penalising malicious use of artificial intelligence and deepfakes (2025, pending); Iniciativa 6626, Personal Data Protection Bill (2025, pending); Iniciativa 6572, Personal Data Protection Bill (2025, pending); Data Protection Bill No. 6,105 (2022, pending); UNESCO Readiness Assessment Methodology report on AI ethics (2026); Estrategia Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial (in preparation)

GIN.name: Guinea

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument is in force, and no regulatory decision applying Loi L/2016/037/AN to AI has been published.
regulation.summary: Guinea regulates AI through strategy rather than law: the Ministry in charge of Posts, Telecommunications and the Digital Economy validated a National Artificial Intelligence Roadmap for 2026-2035 on 20 December 2025, built on the UNDP Artificial Intelligence Landscape Assessment completed in October 2025. The roadmap sets out development, governance and deployment orientations but creates no obligations, and the general framework law Loi L/2016/037/AN on cybersecurity and personal data protection says nothing about AI systems.

promotion.note: A government-UNDP project document on digital innovation and AI signed 15 April 2026 envisages technology hubs and AI deployment, with no disbursed national AI funding, sandbox or AI procurement…

GIN.key_laws: National Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2026-2035 (validated December 2025), Loi L/2016/037/AN relative à la cybersécurité et à la protection des données à caractère personnel (2016), Loi Plan 2026-2040 and Loi-Programme 2026-2030 for the Simandou 2040 programme (2026)

GNB.name: Guinea-Bissau

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument exists, and no regulator has applied general law such as Lei n.º 5/2010 to AI systems.
regulation.summary: Guinea-Bissau has no AI-specific legislation, draft bill or binding instrument. The main digital-policy act is Decreto n.º 10/2025, which approved the Estratégia Nacional para a Transformação Digital (ENTD.GW), launched on 29 January 2025 and focused on connectivity, public-sector digitalisation and cybersecurity rather than AI obligations. Governance capacity has been further disrupted by the military takeover of 26 November 2025 and the transitional administration that followed.

promotion.note: No AI funding programme, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rule exists; donor digital projects under ENTD.GW target connectivity and e-government.

GNB.key_laws: Estratégia Nacional para a Transformação Digital (ENTD.GW), approved by Decreto n.º 10/2025; Lei n.º 5/2010, Lei de Base das Tecnologias de Informação e Comunicação (2010)

GUY.name: Guyana

regulation.binding_note: The only binding instrument reaching AI-related activity is the general Data Protection Act 2023 (No. 18 of 2023), which has no AI-specific provision.
regulation.summary: Guyana has no dedicated AI legislation, no adopted national AI strategy and no AI bill before the National Assembly; AI-relevant rules rest entirely on general instruments, namely the Data Protection Act 2023, the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 2023 and the Open Data Act 2024, none of which mention AI systems. Government activity is concentrated on AI deployment (health diagnostics with Mount Sinai, AI-backed digitisation of the National Insurance Scheme, the Cerebras sovereign AI data centre at Wales) rather than on regulation, and Minister Kwame McCoy told the 152nd Inter-Parliamentary Union Assembly in April 2026 that legislative frameworks still need to be built.

promotion.note: The November 2025 Cerebras memorandum for a 100MW AI data centre at Wales remains an announced project, with no AI fund disbursed, no sandbox and no AI procurement rules.

GUY.key_laws: Data Protection Act 2023 (No. 18 of 2023), Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 2023 (No. 12 of 2023), Open Data Act 2024

HTI.name: Haiti

regulation.binding_note: No binding AI instrument exists; the 2018 data protection arrêté contains no AI provision and no regulator has applied it to AI.
regulation.summary: Haiti has no AI-specific law, decree or regulation, and no AI bill in any legislative process; the Parliament is non-functional and the transitional executive has issued no AI decree. The only texts reaching AI indirectly are the Arrêté of 15 May 2018 on personal data protection and the cyber-offence provisions of the 2020 Penal Code. A national roadmap for responsible AI adoption is being drafted outside government by Banj, the Internet Society Haiti Chapter, the École Supérieure d'Infotronique d'Haïti and the Association for Responsible AI under the Inter-American Development Bank-financed ProAI programme.

promotion.note: ProAI (IDB technical cooperation HA-T1339), launched 11 March 2026 to train 125 professionals, operates alongside the BRH research fund whose 2026 cohort funds AI research.

HTI.key_laws: No AI-specific law, decree or national strategy has been adopted; Arrêté fixant les règles relatives à la protection des données à caractère personnel (2018) and the Code Pénal (2020) cyber-offence provisions are the only general texts touching automated systems, and a national AI roadmap is in preparation under the Programme de création d'opportunités numériques en Haïti par l'intelligence artificielle (ProAI, 2026)

HND.name: Honduras

regulation.binding_note: Consortium Legal's February 2026 Central America review records no AI-specific binding instrument adopted in Honduras.
regulation.summary: Honduras has no AI-specific legislation in force and no comprehensive AI bill before the Congreso Nacional; the Plan Nacional de Gobierno Digital 2023-2026 names AI challenges without creating obligations. The only legislative activity touching AI is a June 2026 proposal to reform the Ley Contra el Acoso Escolar so that AI-generated intimate montages and digital impersonation are punishable, which remains a narrow, unadopted use-case measure.

promotion.note: An IDB-supported DIGER initiative announced in 2026 uses an AI platform to map 365 public procedures, with no AI funding line, sandbox or AI procurement rules.

HND.key_laws: Plan Nacional de Gobierno Digital 2023-2026, Política Nacional de la República Digital 2022-2025, proposed reform to the Ley Contra el Acoso Escolar (Decreto 96-2014) penalising AI-generated content and digital impersonation (bill, 2026)

HUN.name: Hungary

regulation.binding_note: Three AI-specific binding instruments are in force — Regulation 2024/1689, Act LXXV of 2025 and Government Decree 344/2025 (X.31.) — with major high-risk provisions not yet applicable.
regulation.summary: AI regulation rests on the directly applicable EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), implemented nationally by Act LXXV of 2025 and Government Decree 344/2025 (X.31.), in force since 1 December 2025, which designate the AI notifying and market surveillance authorities, fix fine levels in forint and create the Hungarian Artificial Intelligence Council. Coverage is horizontal and the prohibitions, general-purpose AI rules and Article 50 transparency duties apply, but Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI, in force 27 July 2026) pushed Annex III high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 and Annex I systems to 2 August 2028. The regulatory sandbox provisions of Act LXXV entered into force on 2 August 2026 without a published operating sandbox.

promotion.note: Hungary funds the Komondor HPC system and the €42 million EuroHPC LEVENTE supercomputer in Budapest, with no operating AI regulatory sandbox or AI-specific procurement rules published.

ISL.name: Iceland

regulation.binding_note: Only general law, chiefly Act No. 90/2018 on Data Protection, binds AI use; no AI-specific binding instrument is in force.
regulation.summary: Iceland has no AI-specific binding law: the EU AI Act remains under scrutiny for EEA incorporation with a draft Joint Committee Decision pending, so AI is governed by the Act on Data Protection and Processing of Personal Data No. 90/2018 plus the non-binding AI Action Plan 2025-2027. The legislative programme for the 158th session of Althingi (2026-2027) lists a Bill on Deepfakes, banning certain uses of AI in line with European rules, scheduled for November 2026, and the Minister of Culture, Innovation and Higher Education announced consultation on AI legislation in autumn 2026. A draft justice-ministry bill on police use of AI facial recognition was in public discussion in September 2026.

promotion.note: Funding runs through AI Action Plan measures such as grants for health-sector AI and the AI infrastructure action in the Industrial Policy action plan 2026-2027; no sandbox or AI procurement rules…

IND.name: India

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument is in force: the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026.
regulation.summary: India's first binding AI-specific obligations took effect on 20 February 2026 through the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules, 2026, which define synthetically generated information and impose labelling, provenance metadata, user declaration and two-to-three-hour takedown duties on intermediaries. Everything beyond synthetic media remains governed by the non-binding India AI Governance Guidelines (November 2025) with their seven Sutras and by general law including the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. MeitY began consultations in July 2026 on a possible dedicated AI law, and the AI (Ethics and Accountability) Bill, 2025 is an unenacted private member's bill.

promotion.note: IndiaAI Mission funds GPU compute, foundation models and startups, and the Guidelines propose techno-legal sandboxes, with no AI-specific public procurement rules in force.

IND.key_laws: Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules (2026), Information Technology Act (2000), Digital Personal Data Protection Act (2023), Digital Personal Data Protection Rules (2025), India AI Governance Guidelines – Seven Sutras (2025), IndiaAI Mission (2024), New Delhi Declaration on AI Impact (2026), AI Governance and Economic Group (2026)

IDN.name: Indonesia

regulation.binding_note: Only general instruments reach AI: Law No. 27/2022 on Personal Data Protection, Law No. 1/2024 amending the ITE Law and Government Regulation No. 71/2019.
regulation.summary: Indonesia has no enacted binding AI-specific instrument: the two Presidential Regulations on AI Ethics and on the 2026-2029 National AI Roadmap, listed among 46 priority Perpres for 2026, were finalised in draft and sent to the State Secretariat but remained unsigned through September 2026. Governance rests on the non-binding Stranas KA 2020-2045, Komdigi's AI ethics circular and 2025 guidance, OJK's 2025 banking AI governance guidance, and general law on electronic systems and personal data. Derivative rules such as mandatory labelling of AI-generated content are drafted but conditional on the Perpres being issued.

promotion.note: Programs include the AI Center of Excellence launched with Indosat, Cisco and NVIDIA in July 2025 and the UGM Indosat NVIDIA AI Technology Center opened 13 August 2026; no AI procurement rules exist.
