IRN.name: Iran

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument exists, the National AI Development Law (2026); the 2024 National AI Document and 2025 Roadmap are policy documents.
regulation.summary: The National AI Development Law, approved by the Majlis on 19 August 2026, confirmed by the Guardian Council on 26 August 2026 and promulgated by Speaker Ghalibaf on 13 September 2026, is Iran's first binding AI-specific statute; it establishes the National AI Organization under the President, a four-tier risk classification of AI systems, and an AI Security Evaluation and Certification Centre. Operative obligations depend on secondary rules that do not yet exist: the organization's statute is still to be submitted to the Council of Ministers, risk-level criteria and cybersecurity directives are unissued, and Article 12 carves out security and defence bodies. Earlier instruments, the National Artificial Intelligence Document (2024) and the National AI Roadmap (2025), remain policy documents.

promotion.note: The 2026 law creates a National AI Development Fund capitalized at 10,000 billion tomans, alongside state AI R&D and sovereign compute funding announced in 2025.

IRN.key_laws: National AI Development Law (2026), National Artificial Intelligence Document of the Islamic Republic of Iran (2024), National AI Roadmap (2025), Computer Crimes Law (2009)

IRQ.name: Iraq

regulation.binding_note: Only general instruments reach AI: Legislative Order No. 65 of 2004, the Regulation for Organizing Digital Content in Iraq (2023) and Electronic Signature and Electronic Transactions Law No. 78 of…
regulation.summary: Iraq has no enacted AI legislation and no AI-specific binding instrument in force. The Communications and Media Commission opened a 30-day public consultation on 23 September 2026 on a draft Regulatory Framework for Artificial Intelligence Services in the Republic of Iraq, issued under Legislative Order No. 65 of 2004, which proposes risk-tiered licensing, data localisation, user-protection duties and fines up to IQD 200 million. The Iraqi National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence (INSAIN) 2024-2030, reviewed by the Prime Minister-chaired Higher Committee for Artificial Intelligence on 21 August 2024, remains a policy instrument without legal force.

promotion.note: Funding for the national AI strategy was announced alongside a Digital Leaders training cohort and new University of Baghdad AI colleges, with no sandbox or AI procurement rules.

IRL.name: Ireland

regulation.binding_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, S.I. No. 366/2025 and the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Act 2026 are in force, with major AI Act obligations not yet applicable.
regulation.summary: Ireland's framework combines the directly applicable EU AI Act with the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Act 2026, signed on 21 July 2026 and commenced on 31 July 2026, which builds the national supervision, investigation and fining machinery. Prohibitions, AI literacy, general-purpose AI duties and, from 2 August 2026, transparency and penalty provisions apply, while Annex III high-risk obligations were pushed to 2 December 2027 and Annex I products to 2 August 2028 by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. Coverage is horizontal and purpose-built for AI, but the regime is still inside a transition period.

promotion.note: Enterprise Ireland and CeADAR-based AI adoption supports are funded under the National Digital and AI Strategy, while the AI Office states its AI Regulatory Sandbox Programme is under development.

ISR.name: Israel

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument is in force, the 2026 election AI-labelling rules; other duties flow from the general Protection of Privacy Law Amendment 13.
regulation.summary: Israel has no horizontal AI statute; regulation runs through the December 2023 Policy on Artificial Intelligence Regulation and Ethics, sector guidance, and the Protection of Privacy Law 5741-1981 as amended by Amendment 13 (in force 14 August 2025). The one AI-specific binding instrument is the election-propaganda AI disclosure regime effective 26 July 2026, requiring prominent labels on AI-created or AI-altered campaign material. Government Resolution 4255 (16 June 2026) and the National AI Strategic Plan (13 August 2026) concentrate on compute, talent and adoption rather than binding obligations.

promotion.note: Funded programmes include TELEM, Resolution 4255's 100,000-accelerator plan and the Innovation Authority supercomputer, plus an operating AI-in-health regulatory sandbox, while no binding AI…

ITA.name: Italy

regulation.binding_note: Three AI-specific binding instruments apply — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Law No. 132/2025 and Legislative Decree No. 160/2026 — with the AI Act's high-risk regime not yet applicable.
regulation.summary: Italy applies Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 directly and has completed its own national layer: Law No. 132/2025, the first dedicated national AI statute in the EU, and the legislative decrees adopted on 4 August 2026 under Article 24, of which Legislative Decree No. 160 of 9 September 2026 entered into force on 30 September 2026 covering police use of AI, biometric recognition, civil liability and new criminal provisions including Article 437-bis of the Criminal Code. The framework is horizontal and sector-specific at once, reaching healthcare, employment, education, justice, public administration, copyright and deepfakes. Major AI Act obligations for Annex III high-risk systems were postponed to 2 December 2027 by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, and existing police systems have a one-year adaptation period.

promotion.note: A €1 billion CDP Venture Capital AI fund and PNRR programmes operate, and the Italian AI experimentation space run jointly by AgID and ACN was established by the 2026 decree but is not yet admitting…

JAM.name: Jamaica

regulation.binding_note: Only general statutes — the Data Protection Act (2020) and cybercrime legislation — apply to AI; no AI-specific binding instrument is in force.
regulation.summary: Jamaica has no AI-specific binding instrument; the Data Protection Act (2020), the Cybercrimes Act and the Cybercrimes (Amendment) Act (2026) are the general laws that reach AI uses, and the Opposition's push to add express AI and deepfake provisions to the 2026 amendment was not adopted. The National Artificial Intelligence Task Force delivered policy recommendations in 2024 and the UNESCO Readiness Assessment was launched in April 2026, with drafting of a first National AI Policy and public consultation beginning in September 2026.

promotion.note: Minister Wheatley's June 2026 directive on public-service AI literacy announced training measures, with no disbursed AI funding programme, AI procurement rules or AI regulatory sandbox.

JAM.key_laws: Data Protection Act (2020), Cybercrimes Act (2015), Cybercrimes (Amendment) Act (2026), National Artificial Intelligence Policy Recommendations (2024), UNESCO Artificial Intelligence Readiness Assessment Report for Jamaica (2026)

JPN.name: Japan

regulation.binding_note: The AI Promotion Act is the single AI-specific binding statute; the 2026 APPI amendment and Copyright Act Article 30-4 are general law applied to AI.
regulation.summary: Japan's framework rests on the Act on Promotion of Research, Development and Utilization of AI-Related Technologies, a horizontal AI statute in force since 1 September 2025 that creates institutions, effort duties and a cooperation duty rather than enforceable obligations. Implementation is advanced on the policy side, with the AI Basic Plan revised as Phase II on 14 July 2026 and the AI Utilization Guidelines of December 2025 in use, while the July 2026 APPI amendment (Act No. 56 of 2026) adds AI-relevant biometric and children's data rules within general data protection law. Proposals by the Liberal Democratic Party in April 2026 to add penalties for deepfake pornography and AI copyright infringement have not been enacted.

promotion.note: GENIAC compute and semiconductor/data-centre funding run alongside the project-type regulatory sandbox and the Generative AI Procurement Guideline v2.0 in force since 1 September 2026.

JOR.name: Jordan

regulation.binding_note: The CBJ banking AI framework is the one AI-specific instrument binding on private entities; the July 2026 circular binds only government bodies.
regulation.summary: Jordan has no cross-sector AI law; its binding AI layer is sectoral, consisting of the Central Bank of Jordan's Artificial Intelligence Framework for the Banking Sector issued in August 2025 and a Prime Ministry circular of 11 July 2026 barring AI generation or alteration of national emblems, flags and official seals across all government institutions. The economy-wide instruments—the Jordanian Artificial Intelligence Policy (2020), the National Charter of Ethics for Artificial Intelligence (2022) and the Jordanian AI Strategy and Implementation Plan 2023-2027—remain voluntary, and Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 of 2023 contains no AI-specific provision.

promotion.note: Capacity programs such as the "AI for Government Leaders" executive program launched June 2026 and donor-funded strategy projects exist; no AI-specific regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules…

KAZ.name: Kazakhstan

regulation.binding_note: Law No. 230-VIII and Digital Code No. 255-VIII both apply today, with AI offence provisions added to the Code of Administrative Offences by Law No. 232-VIII.
regulation.summary: Law No. 230-VIII 'On Artificial Intelligence', in force since 18 January 2026, sets a risk-based, cross-sector framework with prohibited practices, labelling of AI-generated content, high-risk system duties and liability insurance, and was amended by Law No. 326-VIII of 24 June 2026. The Digital Code No. 255-VIII took effect on 11 July 2026, adding rights to explanation and human review of fully automated decisions. Implementing ministerial orders on AI-system classification criteria and trusted high-risk system lists were issued in April 2026, with further secondary acts still in preparation.

promotion.note: Qazaqstan Venture Group, Astana Hub, Alem.ai and the National AI Platform fund AI work; no operating AI regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules are in place.

KEN.name: Kenya

regulation.binding_note: Only general law binds AI use: the Data Protection Act, 2019, its 2021 General Regulations, and the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, 2018.
regulation.summary: Kenya has no binding AI-specific instrument in force. The Artificial Intelligence Bill, 2026 (Senate Bills No. 4 of 2026), sponsored by Senator Karen Nyamu, was published on 19 February 2026, read a First Time on 2 April 2026, referred to the Senate Standing Committee on Information, Communication and Technology, and sits at Second Reading stage; because it touches county functions it must also clear the National Assembly before assent. Regulation of AI today runs through the Data Protection Act, 2019 and the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner's Guidance Note on Artificial Intelligence (July 2026), which explains existing duties rather than creating AI-specific law.

promotion.note: The National AI Strategy 2025-2030 commits KES 152 billion and the Communications Authority and Capital Markets Authority sandboxes admit AI projects, but no AI procurement rules exist.

KIR.name: Kiribati

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: the Data Protection Act 2025 and Cybercrime Act 2021 contain no AI-specific binding instrument.
regulation.summary: Kiribati regulates the digital sphere through general instruments - the Data Protection Act 2025, Digital Government Act 2023, Electronic Transactions Act 2021 and Cybercrime Act 2021 - none of which creates obligations for AI systems. The closest provision is the Data Protection Act 2025 right against decisions based solely on automated processing, which binds data controllers generally rather than AI developers or deployers. Parliament has no AI bill before it and the government has published no AI strategy.

promotion.note: Donor-funded work such as the World Bank Kiribati Digital Government Project funds connectivity and e-government, with no AI funding scheme, sandbox or AI procurement rule.

XKX.name: Kosovo

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: Law No. 06/L-082 on Personal Data Protection (2019), supervised by the Information and Privacy Agency.
regulation.summary: Kosovo has no AI-specific legislation, and the only law touching AI is Law No. 06/L-082 on Personal Data Protection (2019), which the Information and Privacy Commissioner confirms contains no AI-specific provisions. AI appears only in strategy documents, the e-Government Strategy Kosovo 2023-2027 and the Digital Agenda of Kosovo 2030, as a technology to be piloted in public services. Alignment work with Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 began with a draft impact assessment presented by the Information and Privacy Agency on 27 February 2025 and a readiness assessment started in 2026, but no draft AI law has reached the Assembly.

promotion.note: No AI-targeted funding, procurement rules or sandbox exists; AI features only as a module in EU-funded digital skills training and as a piloting commitment in the e-Government Strategy 2023-2027.

XKX.key_laws: Law No. 06/L-082 on Personal Data Protection (2019), Law No. 06/L-081 on Access to Public Documents (2019), e-Government Strategy Kosovo 2023-2027 (2023), Digital Agenda of Kosovo 2030

KWT.name: Kuwait

regulation.binding_note: Only general instruments apply to AI deployers: CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation (Decision No. 26 of 2024) and Cybercrime Law No. 63 of 2015.
regulation.summary: Kuwait has no AI-specific legislation in force; AI is reached only through general ICT, data-protection and cybercrime instruments. The draft Kuwait National AI Strategy 2025-2028 and CITRA's Guide for Adopting Artificial Intelligence in the State of Kuwait v1.0 set direction without binding anyone, and the parliamentary bill to establish a Public Authority for Artificial Intelligence has not been enacted.

promotion.note: The Central Bank of Kuwait's Wolooj regulatory sandbox runs an Artificial Intelligence in Finance cohort and CAIT runs a national AI and cloud skilling programme with Microsoft.

KWT.key_laws: Kuwait National AI Strategy 2025-2028 (draft), Guide for Adopting Artificial Intelligence in the State of Kuwait v1.0 (CITRA, 2026), CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation (Decision No. 26 of 2024), Cybercrime Law No. 63 of 2015, National Cybersecurity Center (Decision No. 37 of 2022), Kuwait Vision 2035 (2017), draft bill establishing the Public Authority for Artificial Intelligence

KGZ.name: Kyrgyzstan

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument is in force: the artificial intelligence chapter of the Digital Code, applicable since 6 February 2026.
regulation.summary: The Digital Code of the Kyrgyz Republic (Law No. 178 of 31 July 2025), brought into force on 6 February 2026 by Law No. 179, defines AI systems and AI systems of heightened danger, sets principles for their design, development and application, imposes restrictions and liability, and grants a right to human review of algorithmic and automated decisions. These binding provisions apply across sectors but depend on secondary acts that are still at draft stage, and no standalone AI statute has been tabled in the Jogorku Kenesh.

promotion.note: The Concept of Digital Transformation for 2024-2028 announces a National AI Platform and AI competence centres, and construction of a National AI Centre was announced for 2026, with no disbursed…

KGZ.key_laws: Digital Code of the Kyrgyz Republic (Law No. 178 of 31 July 2025, in force 6 February 2026), Law on Enactment of the Digital Code of the Kyrgyz Republic (No. 179 of 31 July 2025), Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 29 of 22 January 2025 on the National Council on Artificial Intelligence Development (as amended by Resolution No. 844 of 29 December 2025), Concept of Digital Transformation of the Kyrgyz Republic for 2024-2028, draft Regulation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2026)

LAO.name: Laos

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument exists, and no regulator has applied the Law on Cyber Crime (2015) or Law on Electronic Data Protection (2017) to AI systems.
regulation.summary: Laos has no binding AI rule in force, before the National Assembly, or formally proposed. The only AI-specific document is the draft National Strategy on Artificial Intelligence 2026-2035, which the government approved in principle at its September 2026 monthly meeting and sent back to the Ministry of Technology and Communications for revision on infrastructure, databases, personnel and priority applications. General ICT instruments, namely the Law on Telecommunications (2011), Law on Electronic Transactions (2012, amended 2022), Law on Cyber Crime (2015) and Law on Electronic Data Protection (2017), address AI nowhere in their text.

promotion.note: The 2026-2030 investment plan designates AI and data centres as priority sectors for investment promotion, with no disbursed AI funding program, sandbox or AI procurement rule.

LAO.key_laws: Draft National Strategy on Artificial Intelligence 2026-2035 (approved in principle September 2026), AI Ethics Readiness Assessment Methodology Country Report (2026), National Digital Economy Strategy (2024), Law on Electronic Data Protection (2017), Law on Cyber Crime (2015), Law on Electronic Transactions (2012, amended 2022), Law on Telecommunications (2011)

LVA.name: Latvia

regulation.binding_note: AI Centre Law (2025), Financial Market Digital Operational Resilience and AI Use Law (1 October 2025) and Criminal Law Section 90.1 on election deepfakes apply, while AI Act high-risk duties are…
regulation.summary: Latvia applies the EU AI Act directly, with prohibitions, general-purpose AI rules and Article 50 transparency obligations applying and Annex III high-risk duties postponed to December 2027 by the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744). National legislation adds the Law on the Latvian Artificial Intelligence Centre, amended on 14 May 2026, and the Financial Market Digital Operational Resilience and Artificial Intelligence Use Law in force since 1 October 2025, alongside Criminal Law deepfake provisions. Competent authorities were allocated by Cabinet-level informative report rather than by a general implementing statute, and sandbox secondary rules and Centre operations lag.

promotion.note: The AI Centre opened a project call for its special regulatory environment in 2026 and runs AI Factory antenna work, with no AI procurement rules adopted.

LVA.key_laws: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, 2024), Digital Omnibus on Artificial Intelligence (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, 2026), Law on the Latvian Artificial Intelligence Centre (Mākslīgā intelekta centra likums, 2025) with amendments of 14 May 2026, Financial Market Digital Operational Resilience and Artificial Intelligence Use Law (Finanšu tirgus digitālās darbības noturības un mākslīgā intelekta izmantošanas likums, 2025), Criminal Law Section 90.1 on influencing the election process using deepfake technology (2024), Digital Transformation Guidelines 2021-2027 (2020), National AI Strategy 'Par mākslīgā intelekta risinājumu attīstību' (2020)

LBN.name: Lebanon

regulation.binding_note: Only general law applies, chiefly Law No. 81/2018 on Electronic Transactions and Personal Data; no AI-specific binding instrument is in force.
regulation.summary: Lebanon has no binding AI legislation. Governance rests on the National Digital Transformation and Artificial Intelligence Strategy launched on 7 November 2025 by the Office of the Minister of State for Information Technology and Artificial Intelligence, a Cabinet-approved draft law to create a Ministry of Technology and Artificial Intelligence referred to joint parliamentary committees in July 2026, and a draft Digital Authority law. AI-related conduct falls under general instruments, principally Law No. 81/2018 on Electronic Transactions and Personal Data, which contains no AI-specific provision.

promotion.note: The NUMŪ national digital and AI capacity-building platform and the UAE-backed 'One Million Lebanese AI Experts' initiative launched 25 September 2026 operate, with no sandbox or AI procurement rules.

LBN.key_laws: National Digital Transformation and Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2025), Draft Law establishing the Ministry of Technology and Artificial Intelligence (MITAI) (2025, pending before Parliament), Draft Digital Authority Law (2025, pending before Parliament), Law No. 81/2018 on Electronic Transactions and Personal Data

LSO.name: Lesotho

regulation.binding_note: The only binding instruments reaching AI are general: the Data Protection Act 2011 and the Lesotho Communications Authority Act (2012).
regulation.summary: Lesotho governs AI through a non-binding national policy instrument, the Artificial Intelligence Policy and Implementation Plan (2025), led by the Ministry of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation, alongside general law in the Data Protection Act 2011 (Act No. 5 of 2012) and sector powers of the Lesotho Communications Authority. In August 2026 the Ministry and the United Nations ran a five-day Maseru workshop to develop a National AI Strategy and Data Centre Blueprint, and in September 2026 Lesotho became the first country to apply the United Nations Blueprint for National AI and Data Strategies. No binding AI obligation, high-risk duty or AI regulator exists in law, and the Cybercrime Bill 2026 and Cybersecurity Bill 2026 remain in stakeholder consultation.

promotion.note: Phase One of the National Compute Roadmap 2026-2029 was announced without published budget or cost estimate, and no AI funding program, sandbox or AI procurement rule exists.

LSO.key_laws: Artificial Intelligence Policy and Implementation Plan (2025, draft), Data Protection Act 2011 (Act No. 5 of 2012), Lesotho Communications Authority Act (2012), ICT Policy (2005), Cybercrime Bill 2026 (pending), Cybersecurity Bill 2026 (pending)

LBR.name: Liberia

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument exists, and no regulator has applied the Data Protection Act (2026) or Cybercrime Act (2026) to AI systems.
regulation.summary: Liberia has no dedicated AI legislation, no national AI strategy and no binding AI-specific instrument. The legal base built in 2026 is general: President Joseph Boakai signed the Cybercrime Act and the Data Protection Act of Liberia, and the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications issued the "Whole of Government" National Digital Strategy (2025-2029) and a Draft National Data Governance Policy (2026), none of which regulates AI systems, models or outputs.

promotion.note: AI activity is donor-run capacity building — the UNDP-supported AI Training Programme for government officials (November 2025) and UNDP AI Sprint — with no national funding scheme, AI procurement…

LBR.key_laws: Data Protection Act of Liberia (2026), Cybercrime Act (2026), "Whole of Government" National Digital Strategy (2025-2029), Draft National Data Governance Policy (2026), National Cybersecurity Strategy (2025-2029)

LBY.name: Libya

regulation.binding_note: Law No. 5 of 2022 Regarding Combating Cybercrimes and Law No. 6 of 2022 Concerning Electronic Transactions are the only binding instruments reaching AI-related conduct; neither is AI-specific.
regulation.summary: Libya has no binding AI legislation. Governance rests on two non-binding instruments: the National Artificial Intelligence Policy launched by the General Authority for Communications and Informatics on 17 May 2024, and the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026-2030 with the National Charter for Artificial Intelligence Ethics adopted in Tripoli on 1 June 2026, whose legislation-and-ethics pillar only promises a future legal framework.

promotion.note: The 2026-2030 strategy promises AI incubators, scholarships and support for 100 startups by 2030, with no funded program, sandbox or AI procurement rule in operation.

LBY.key_laws: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026-2030 (2026), National Charter for Artificial Intelligence Ethics (2026), National Artificial Intelligence Policy of the State of Libya (2024), Law No. 5 of 2022 Regarding Combating Cybercrimes, Law No. 6 of 2022 Concerning Electronic Transactions

LIE.name: Liechtenstein

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI - the Datenschutzgesetz, criminal and personality law - with no AI-specific binding instrument in force.
regulation.summary: Liechtenstein has no AI-specific binding legislation in force: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and its amending Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI, 8 July 2026) are marked EEA-relevant but remain under scrutiny by the EEA EFTA states, and the government states in BuA Nr. 34/2026 that both the AI Act and the Digital Services Act will apply directly only after EEA incorporation. The sole domestic AI-specific instrument is the non-binding KI-Strategie der Liechtensteinischen Landesverwaltung adopted on 14 April 2026, which governs the administration's own use and imposes mandatory staff training. AI in the market is reached only through general instruments: the Datenschutzgesetz, financial-market rules, and the criminal, media and personality law catalogue described in the deepfake Postulat response.

promotion.note: No regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules exist; AI measures are confined to internal training and centrally bundled AI tools under the 2026 administration strategy.

LIE.key_laws: EU AI Act / Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (2024, pending EEA incorporation), Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 Digital Omnibus on AI (2026, under EEA EFTA scrutiny), KI-Strategie der Liechtensteinischen Landesverwaltung (2026, non-binding), Postulatsbeantwortung betreffend Massnahmen gegen Missbrauch durch Deepfakes BuA Nr. 34/2026 (2026), Interpellationsbeantwortung betreffend Künstliche Intelligenz, Cloud-Computing und technologische Infrastruktur BuA Nr. 59/2026 (2026), Datenschutzgesetz (2019), Cyber-Sicherheitsgesetz LGBl. 2025/111 (2025), Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence CETS 225 (signed 2025)

LTU.name: Lithuania

regulation.binding_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, plus laws XV-105 and XV-106 in force since 1 April 2025, are AI-specific and binding, with high-risk provisions not yet applying.
regulation.summary: Lithuania governs AI through the directly applicable EU AI Act, whose prohibitions, AI literacy, GPAI and Article 50 transparency and marking obligations apply, while Annex III high-risk obligations were pushed to 2 December 2027 by the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744). National implementation rests on the January 2025 amendments to the Law on Technology and Innovation (XV-105) and the Law on Information Society Services (XV-106), effective 1 April 2025, which named the Communications Regulatory Authority (RRT) as market surveillance authority and single point of contact and the Innovation Agency as notifying authority. A dedicated Law on Implementation of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, distributing high-risk supervision across eleven bodies and setting complaint, investigation and liability procedures, remains in the Seimas.

promotion.note: The Innovation Agency runs a €3 million AI regulatory sandbox and over €42 million of Lithuanian-language AI resources, a €7.5 million SME adoption scheme and the €65 million LitAI hub are funded…

LTU.key_laws: EU AI Act / Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (2024), Digital Omnibus on AI / Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (2026), Law on Technology and Innovation amendments No. XV-105 (2025), Law on Information Society Services amendments No. XV-106 (2025), Draft Law on Implementation of the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act (2026), National Artificial Intelligence Strategic Guidelines 2026-2035 (2026), Lithuanian Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2019), AI Strategy Action Plan 2023-2026

LUX.name: Luxembourg

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument applies, the EU AI Act as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744; the DSA and GPSR implementing laws of 2025 are not AI-specific.
regulation.summary: Luxembourg's binding AI framework is the directly applicable EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), whose prohibitions and AI literacy duty have applied since February 2025 and general-purpose AI obligations since August 2025, while Annex III high-risk requirements were deferred to 2 December 2027 by the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744). The national implementing instrument, Bill of Law 8476 filed on 23 December 2024, designating competent authorities and national penalties, remains in committee after Conseil d'État objections on arbitration between authorities. The CNPD acts as de facto coordinator pending that adoption.

promotion.note: MeluXina-AI AI Factory, the Mistral AI partnership and the CNPD/AI Factory ReMI regulatory sandbox pilot operate, with no AI-specific public procurement rules published.

LUX.key_laws: EU AI Act / Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (2024), Digital Omnibus on AI / Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (2026), Bill of Law No. 8476 implementing the AI Act (2024, pending), Accelerating Digital Sovereignty 2030 – National AI Strategy (2025), Law of 4 April 2025 implementing the Digital Services Act, Law of 28 February 2025 implementing the General Product Safety Regulation, Bill of Law No. 8364 transposing NIS2 (2024)

MKD.name: Macedonia

regulation.binding_note: The Law on Personal Data Protection (2020) is the only binding instrument reaching AI, and it contains no AI-specific obligation.
regulation.summary: No dedicated AI statute, adopted national AI strategy or binding AI rule exists; AI is governed indirectly through the GDPR-aligned Law on Personal Data Protection (2020) and framed by the non-binding ICT Development Strategy SMART/MK 2030 (2025). A first draft National Artificial Intelligence Strategy was discussed by the Ministry of Digital Transformation working group on 18 September 2026 for publication on the ENER consultation portal, with adoption targeted for end-2026 and a separate law on AI use announced as a follow-up activity. The Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence (CETS No. 225), signed on 8 May 2026, is not yet ratified or transposed.

promotion.note: The Vezilka National Centre for Artificial Intelligence, co-financed by the Ministry of Digital Transformation and FINKI as a EuroHPC AI Factory Antenna, launched in October 2025.

MKD.key_laws: Law on Personal Data Protection / ZZLP (2020), ICT Development Strategy SMART/MK 2030 (2025), Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law CETS No. 225 (signed 8 May 2026), draft National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence (2026), State Audit Office performance audit report on the possibility of using artificial intelligence in the public sector (2025)

MDG.name: Madagascar

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument exists, and no regulator has applied Loi n° 2014-038 or Loi n° 2014-006 to AI systems.
regulation.summary: Madagascar has no AI-specific legislation and none in the legislative process. Governance of AI falls back on general instruments — Loi n° 2014-038 du 9 janvier 2015 sur la protection des données à caractère personnel with its Décret d'application n° 2023-1541, and Loi n° 2014-006 sur la lutte contre la cybercriminalité — none of which addresses AI systems, and the data protection authority they establish is not yet operational.

promotion.note: An International AI Institute for the Indian Ocean with France was announced as a public-private project; no regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules exist.

MDG.key_laws: Loi n° 2014-038 du 9 janvier 2015 sur la protection des données à caractère personnel (2014), Décret n° 2023-1541 d'application de la loi n° 2014-038 (2023), Loi n° 2014-006 sur la lutte contre la cybercriminalité (2014), Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028

MWI.name: Malawi

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: the Data Protection Act (2024) and Electronic Transactions and Cyber Security Act (2016), neither containing AI provisions.
regulation.summary: Malawi has no AI-specific binding instrument; the Electronic Transactions and Cyber Security Act (2016) and the Data Protection Act (2024), in force since 3 June 2024 with MACRA as data protection authority, are the only laws reaching AI and contain no AI provisions. A National Artificial Intelligence Strategy and an accompanying AI Bill covering government and private-sector AI use are in drafting under the Ministry of Information and Communications Technology, with the bill announced for tabling before December 2026.

promotion.note: MACRA launched a regulatory sandbox in September 2025 open to local startups testing emerging technologies including artificial intelligence.

MWI.key_laws: Electronic Transactions and Cyber Security Act (2016), Data Protection Act (2024), Draft National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2026), draft Artificial Intelligence Bill (2026)

MYS.name: Malaysia

regulation.binding_note: Only general instruments apply to AI, including the Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2024 and Cybersecurity Act 2024; no AI-specific binding instrument is in force.
regulation.summary: Malaysia has no binding AI-specific legislation in force. The AI Governance Bill, drafted by the Ministry of Digital and the National AI Office, went through public consultation from 10 to 31 July 2026 and is now expected in the Dewan Rakyat in early 2027 with a risk-based design; the Cybercrimes Bill 2026, passed by the Dewan Rakyat on 1 July 2026 and the Dewan Negara on 20 July 2026, creates offences for deepfakes and digitally manipulated intimate images but awaits royal assent and a commencement date. AI is otherwise governed by general law and by the non-binding National Guidelines on AI Governance and Ethics (2024) and MY-AI Standards platform.

promotion.note: MDEC's AI Sandbox pilot programme, AI talent and startup funding and the National AI Action Plan 2026-2030's 28 initiatives operate without a regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules in force.

MYS.key_laws: National AI Roadmap (AI-Rmap 2021-2025), National Guidelines on AI Governance and Ethics (AIGE 2024), Cybersecurity Act 2024, Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2024, Online Safety Act (Act 866, in force 1 January 2026), MY-AI Standards Platform (2026), National AI Action Plan 2026-2030, Cybercrimes Bill 2026 (passed by both Houses July 2026, not yet in operation), proposed AI Governance Bill (public consultation July 2026)

MDV.name: Maldives

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument exists; the ICT Act (2017) and Maldives Media and Broadcasting Regulation Act (Act No. 16/2025) contain no AI provisions.
regulation.summary: Maldives has no binding AI-specific legislation; the National AI Masterplan 2025–2035, announced by President Mohamed Muizzu in October 2024 and recommended for finalisation by the UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment Report of 31 July 2025, is still in draft. Legislative activity in 2026 under the Maldives 2.0 agenda covers data protection, digital identity and digital transformation rather than AI systems, leaving AI addressed only incidentally through general digital and media law.

promotion.note: The Maldives AI Lab / National AI and Data Competency Centre, set up by MINDCo with Bank of Maldives, was launched in May 2026 alongside the Co.Lab 2026 programme.

MDV.key_laws: National AI Masterplan 2025–2035 (draft, announced 2024), UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment Report for Maldives (2025), Maldives Communications Authority / ICT Act (2017), Privacy and Personal Data Protection Bill (submitted to the People's Majlis, 2026), Maldives 2.0 Digital Transformation Bill (2026), Digital Identity Bill (2026), Maldives Media and Broadcasting Regulation Act (Act No. 16/2025)

MLI.name: Mali

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument is in force: Ordonnance n°2023-022/PT-RM (2023) creating CIAR-Mali, with its implementing decree of August 2023.
regulation.summary: Mali's only AI-specific legal text is Ordonnance n°2023-022/PT-RM of 4 August 2023 creating the Centre d'Intelligence Artificielle et de Robotique du Mali (CIAR-Mali) as a public scientific and technological establishment, ratified by the Conseil national de Transition in October 2023 and implemented by a decree on the centre's organisation and functioning. That text establishes a training and research body and imposes no obligations on AI developers or users, and no AI bill, decree or regulation governing AI systems has been tabled. General law, chiefly Loi n°2013-015 of 21 May 2013 on personal data protection, contains no provision written for AI.

promotion.note: The state financed and opened the CFA 3.3 billion CIAR-Mali campus at Kati-Sirakoro Niaré on 21 September 2026, with a first intake of 40 students for 2026-2027.

MLI.key_laws: Ordonnance n°2023-022/PT-RM du 04 août 2023 portant création du Centre d'Intelligence Artificielle et de Robotique du Mali (2023), Décret n°2023-0420/PT-RM fixant l'organisation et les modalités de fonctionnement du CIAR-Mali (2023), Loi n°2013-015 du 21 mai 2013 portant protection des données à caractère personnel (2013, amended 2017), Politique Nationale de Développement de l'Économie Numérique (2024)

MLT.name: Malta

regulation.binding_note: Three AI-specific binding instruments are in force — the EU AI Act, Legal Notice 226 of 2025 and Legal Notice 227 of 2025 — with high-risk provisions not yet applicable.
regulation.summary: Malta's binding framework is the EU AI Act, operationalised nationally by Legal Notice 226 of 2025 (Artificial Intelligence Regulations) and Legal Notice 227 of 2025 designating the Information and Data Protection Commissioner. Prohibitions, general-purpose AI duties, AI literacy and Article 50 transparency obligations apply, while stand-alone high-risk obligations were pushed to 2 December 2027 by the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744). Coverage is horizontal and cross-sectoral, with the national sandbox and high-risk supervision still being built out.

promotion.note: MDIA runs the Technology Assurance Sandbox and EU-funded AI pilots (GovTech4All local councils call, 2026), while the AI Act regulatory sandbox is required only by 2 August 2027.

MLT.key_laws: EU AI Act / Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (2024), Digital Omnibus on AI / Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (2026), Artificial Intelligence Regulations – Legal Notice 226 of 2025 (S.L. 591.05), Artificial Intelligence (Designation of the Information and Data Protection Commissioner for the purposes of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) Regulations – Legal Notice 227 of 2025, Malta Digital Innovation Authority (Amendment) Act XIX (2024), Malta Digital Innovation Authority Act (Cap. 592, 2018), The Ultimate AI Launchpad: A Strategy and Vision for Artificial Intelligence in Malta 2030 (2019), MGA–MDIA AI Gaming Charter (2026)

MHL.name: Marshall Islands

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument exists, and no regulator has applied general law such as the Cybercrimes Act 2025 to AI systems.
regulation.summary: The Republic of the Marshall Islands has no AI-specific legislation in force or in the legislative process. Technology-related statutes on the Nitijela register are general in character: the Cybercrimes Act 2025 (31 MIRC Ch. 5) criminalises computer-related forgery and offences involving adapted or modified depictions without naming artificial intelligence, and there is no general personal data protection law or data protection authority. Leaders endorsed regional AI principles in September 2026, but nothing binding has followed domestically.

promotion.note: No AI funding scheme, AI procurement rule or regulatory sandbox exists; the World Bank-financed Digital RMI Project covers connectivity and telecommunications reform only.

MHL.key_laws: Pacific Digital and Artificial Intelligence Technology Principles (2026, regional instrument endorsed by the Republic of the Marshall Islands at the Fifty-Fifth Pacific Islands Forum), Cybercrimes Act 2025 (31 MIRC Ch. 5, general cybercrime law with no AI provision)

MRT.name: Mauritania

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument exists; the only national AI document is the non-binding National AI Strategy 2024-2029.
regulation.summary: Mauritania governs AI through the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Mauritania 2024-2029, prepared by the Ministry of Digital Transformation, Innovation and Modernization of Administration, which sets five priorities including data governance and ethical AI but creates no obligations. No AI-specific statute, decree or regulation is in force or before the National Assembly, and Law No. 2017-020 on the protection of personal data addresses automated processing without any AI-specific provision.

promotion.note: Additional World Bank financing under the West Africa Regional Digital Integration Program to cover AI data infrastructure and skills was agreed in June 2026; no sandbox or AI procurement rules exist.

MRT.key_laws: National Artificial Intelligence Strategy of Mauritania 2024-2029 (2024), Law No. 2017-020 on the Protection of Personal Data (2017)

MUS.name: Mauritius

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument regulates conduct: the Financial Services (Robotic and Artificial Intelligence Enabled Advisory Services) Rules 2021.
regulation.summary: Mauritius has no horizontal binding AI legislation; the National AI Strategy 2025-2029 and the FAIR Guidelines launched on 10 April 2026 are explicitly non-binding. The only binding AI-specific instrument remains the Financial Services (Robotic and Artificial Intelligence Enabled Advisory Services) Rules 2021, supplemented by the Financial Services Commission's non-binding Fintech Series Guidance Notes No. 4 on the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Financial Services of September 2025. The Data Protection Act 2017 applies to AI only incidentally, and the Economic and Financial Measures (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2026 addresses AI through an investment scheme rather than conduct rules.

promotion.note: Rs 25 million Public Sector AI Programme, AI Innovation Start-Up Programme tax deductions and the statutory AI City Scheme in the Economic and Financial Measures (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2026…

MUS.key_laws: National AI Strategy (2018), Data Protection Act (2017), Financial Services (Robotic and Artificial Intelligence Enabled Advisory Services) Rules (2021), Digital Transformation Blueprint 2025-2029, FSC Fintech Series Guidance Notes No. 4 on the Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence in Financial Services (2025), National AI Strategy 2025-2029, FAIR Guidelines (2026), Economic and Financial Measures (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2026 (AI City Scheme)

MEX.name: Mexico

regulation.binding_note: The 14 May 2026 labour and copyright reform is the single enacted AI-specific binding instrument; INE lineamientos bind only the electoral sphere.
regulation.summary: No general AI law is in force: the Ley Nacional para Regular el Uso de la Inteligencia Artificial (11 February 2026) and the Senate Science and Technology Committee's draft general AI law announced on 30 April 2026 remain in committee. Binding AI provisions exist only inside adapted general law—the 14 May 2026 reforms to the Ley Federal del Trabajo and Ley Federal del Derecho de Autor against voice and image cloning, and the 2025 LFPDPPP rules on automated decision-making—supplemented by Instituto Nacional Electoral guidelines restricting AI and deepfakes in electoral propaganda.

promotion.note: The ATDT runs a public AI training school and launched an AI Factory with 20 specialists building customs, invoicing and patent models, announced 1 October 2026; no AI regulatory sandbox operates.

MEX.key_laws: Reformas a la Ley Federal del Trabajo y a la Ley Federal del Derecho de Autor en materia de inteligencia artificial (2026), Ley Federal de Protección de Datos Personales en Posesión de los Particulares (2025), Ley Federal de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión (2025), Plan Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial (2026), Principios Chapultepec (2026), Propuesta de Agenda Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial 2024-2030, Lineamientos y principios para el desarrollo estratégico y uso regulado de la inteligencia artificial en el Instituto Nacional Electoral (INE/JGE175/2025), Ley Nacional para Regular el Uso de la Inteligencia Artificial (draft, 2026)

regulation.summary: The Federated States of Micronesia has no AI-specific legislation, no binding AI rules, and no formal AI governance framework in force or under active consideration as of mid-2026. The country remains focused on foundational connectivity and digital infrastructure challenges rather than AI regulation.

MDA.name: Moldova

regulation.binding_note: Law No. 195/2024 on Personal Data Protection is general law; the only AI-written provisions sit inside an education integrity regulation, not a dedicated AI instrument.
regulation.summary: Moldova has no dedicated AI law; the only binding rules written for AI are the Framework Regulation on Academic Integrity in Higher Education Institutions approved on 24 June 2026, which defines unauthorised use of generative AI as misconduct and requires students to declare AI use, together with the Ministry of Education and Research anti-plagiarism methodological standards. Law No. 195/2024 on Personal Data Protection, in force since 23 August 2026, applies to AI only indirectly, and the Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI (CETS No. 225) remains signed but unratified. The National Programme on Artificial Intelligence and Data Management 2026–2030 and Central Electoral Commission amendments covering AI in online campaigns are still drafts.

promotion.note: Moldova AI Hub consortium signed 26 September 2026 and the EU-funded FAIMA AI antenna (€5 million, PIAST AI Factory access) operate; no AI sandbox or AI procurement rules exist.

MDA.key_laws: White Paper on Data Management and Artificial Intelligence (2024), Framework Regulation on Academic Integrity in Higher Education Institutions (2026), Methodological Anti-Plagiarism Standards for Higher Education Institutions (2026), Law No. 195/2024 on Personal Data Protection (in force 23 August 2026), Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (CETS No. 225) – signature 2024, draft National Programme on Artificial Intelligence and Data Management 2026–2030, National Smart Specialisation Programme "Smart Moldova" 2024–2027 (Government Decision No. 588/2024)

MCO.name: Monaco

regulation.binding_note: Only general law applies to AI: Law No. 1.565 (2024) on personal data protection and Law No. 1.383 for a Digital Principality.
regulation.summary: Monaco has no AI statute in force; AI is reached only through Law No. 1.565 of 3 December 2024 on the protection of personal data, enforced by the Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles. Two AI-relevant texts are in the legislative pipeline: Projet de loi n° 1.087 on video protection and remote biometric identification, which expressly builds on artificial-intelligence image processing and was still awaiting debate in 2026, and Proposition de loi n° 281 on online hate content, adopted by the Conseil National on 29 June 2026, which defines deepfakes.

promotion.note: Extended Monaco Enterprises and its Digital FlashUp scheme fund business digital and AI upskilling; no regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules exist.

MNG.name: Mongolia

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: the Law of Mongolia on Personal Data Protection (2021), which the 2025 national AI strategy directs AI systems to comply with.
regulation.summary: Mongolia governs AI through policy rather than law: the National Strategy on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence was adopted by Government Resolution No. 108 in September 2025 alongside the Digital First policy, and 2026 was declared the Year of Big Data and AI. No binding AI-specific instrument is in force; a Law on Artificial Intelligence is being drafted jointly by the Ministry of Digital Development, Innovation and Communications and the Ministry of Justice and Home Affairs but has not reached the State Great Khural. AI use is reached only by general law, principally the Law on Personal Data Protection (2021).

promotion.note: A three-year AI and big data skills program with Oracle runs under an MoU with the ministry, alongside planned GPU-cluster AI Centre and National Data Repository investments.

MNG.key_laws: National Strategy on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (2025, Government Resolution No. 108), Digital First policy (2025), Digital Nation Strategy, Law of Mongolia on Personal Data Protection (2021), Five-Year Development Guidelines of Mongolia for 2026-2030 (2025), draft Law on Artificial Intelligence (in preparation, 2025-2026)

MNE.name: Montenegro

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI, principally the Personal Data Protection Act (2023) and the Criminal Code of Montenegro.
regulation.summary: No AI-specific binding instrument is in force, and the National AI Strategy 2026-2030 with its 2026 Action Plan is still being drafted by the Working Group coordinated by the Ministry of Public Administration. The Ministry of Justice has announced separate legislation on the misuse of AI, drafted with Italian assistance, with no text before Parliament. Personal data protection, copyright and criminal law apply to AI only incidentally.

promotion.note: MontEDIH under Digital Europe, NCC Montenegro/EuroCC HPC support and the judiciary's first AI server acquired in March 2026 are funded programmes without a sandbox.

MAR.name: Morocco

regulation.binding_note: Binding AI provisions exist only in the electoral package (Organic Law 53.25 and HACA decision 50-26); other applicable texts are general data-protection and cybersecurity law.
regulation.summary: Morocco's only binding AI rules sit inside electoral law: Organic Law 53.25 amending Organic Law 27.11 introduced article 51-bis penalising dissemination of falsified or AI-generated content and banning electoral material on AI tools on polling day, and HACA's Superior Council decision 50-26 of 16 June 2026 prohibits deceptive AI-generated electoral content and requires permanent labelling of AI-generated broadcast material. Outside elections, AI is governed by general law — Law No. 09-08 on personal data applied by the CNDP and Law No. 05-20 on cybersecurity applied by the DGSSI. The cross-sector Digital X.0 framework law remains under review at the General Secretariat of the Government and the bill creating a National AI Agency has not been adopted.

promotion.note: Funded initiatives include the JAZARI ROOT Institute centre of excellence, national digital and AI training programmes, and the Mistral AI multilingual model lab partnership.

MOZ.name: Mozambique

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument is in force: Decree No. 14/2026 of 17 April creating the CNIA.
regulation.summary: Mozambique's only binding AI-specific instrument is Decree No. 14/2026 of 17 April 2026, which creates the National Commission for Artificial Intelligence (CNIA) as a consultative and technical advisory body reporting to the Council of Ministers; it imposes no duties on developers or users of AI. The National AI Strategy (ENIA) remains a draft after public consultation from 4 May to 4 June 2026 and continued stakeholder engagement through October 2026, and the Ministry of Education and Culture is drafting rules on AI in education for submission to the Council of Ministers before the end of 2026. The Cybersecurity Law and Cybercrime Law approved in 2026 and the Personal Data Protection Bill approved by the Council of Ministers on 3 March 2026 contain no AI-specific provisions.

promotion.note: ITU approved support for an AI Regulatory Sandbox under 'AI Sandbox for Good' and INTIC signed an MoU with INS for a public-health AI sandbox, both still in preparation.

MMR.name: Myanmar

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: Cybersecurity Law No. 1/2025 and the Telecommunications Law contain no AI-specific obligation.
regulation.summary: Myanmar has no AI-specific legislation in force and none in the legislative process; the National AI Strategy (2025-2030) and National AI Policy drafted by the Ministry of Science and Technology since 2025 remain unpublished and unadopted. Cybersecurity Law No. 1/2025, in force since 30 July 2025, defines artificial intelligence and licenses digital platforms and cybersecurity service providers, but imposes no duty on AI developers or deployers. Regional assessments place Myanmar, with Cambodia and Lao PDR, among ASEAN members without a dedicated national AI strategy or agency.

promotion.note: The Ministry of Education announced on 24 April 2026 AI-driven Centres for Research and Innovation at Naypyitaw State Academy, University of Yangon and University of Mandalay, with no sandbox or AI…

MMR.key_laws: Cybersecurity Law No. 1/2025, draft National AI Strategy (2025-2030) and National AI Policy, Digital Economy Development Master Plan (2021-2025)

NAM.name: Namibia

regulation.binding_note: Only general instruments such as the Communications Act (2009) reach AI conduct; the Data Protection Bill and Cybercrime Bill remain unenacted drafts.
regulation.summary: Namibia has no binding AI-specific instrument; the Artificial Intelligence Readiness Assessment Report (2025) confirms the absence of AI legislation, and the Ministry of Information and Communication Technology has stated an Artificial Intelligence Act is being developed but not yet tabled. The draft National Artificial Intelligence Strategy, prepared by the National Commission on Research, Science and Technology with UNESCO, the United Nations Development Programme and the Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung, was at national validation stage in September 2026. AI-related harms such as deepfake scams are handled through general communications and criminal law and public advisories rather than AI-written rules.

promotion.note: No regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules exist; the National Data Centre adjoining the AI Institute is under construction.

NAM.key_laws: Artificial Intelligence Readiness Assessment Report (2025), draft National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2026), National Digital Strategy, Cybercrime Bill (2026, draft), Data Protection Bill (draft), Communications Act (2009), National Digital Economy Roadmap (2022)

NRU.name: Nauru

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument is in force, and no general law has been applied to AI by a Nauruan regulator.
regulation.summary: Nauru has no AI-specific legislation, bill or national AI strategy; the Nauru National Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030 addresses connectivity, digital services, planned data-protection and cybersecurity legislation, without AI provisions. Artificial intelligence is touched only incidentally by the Cybercrime Act 2015 and the Communications and Broadcasting Act 2018, neither of which contains any AI-written rule.

promotion.note: No AI funding program, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rule exists; the Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030 funds connectivity and e-government only.

NRU.key_laws: Nauru National Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030 (2025), Cybercrime Act 2015, Communications and Broadcasting Act 2018, Pacific Digital and Artificial Intelligence Technology Principles (2026, regional, endorsed by Pacific Islands Forum Leaders)

NPL.name: Nepal

regulation.binding_note: No standalone AI-specific binding instrument exists; AI duties appear only as provisions within the Election Code of Conduct 2082 and general law such as the Individual Privacy Act 2075.
regulation.summary: Nepal governs AI chiefly through the cabinet-approved National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy 2082 of August 2025, a non-binding strategy that promises AI legislation and an AI Regulation Council. The only binding AI-written rules sit inside the Election Code of Conduct 2082, in force since 18 January 2026, which prohibits AI-generated misinformation and deepfakes in election campaigning and carries fines and candidacy cancellation. A dedicated AI bill appears in the government's legislative plan for fiscal year 2026-27 and the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation has approved a concept paper for an umbrella Science, Technology and Innovation Bill covering AI and robotics, but neither has reached parliament.

promotion.note: Regulatory sandboxes, AI incubation hubs and provincial AI Excellence Centres promised in National AI Policy 2082 remain unfunded and unopened.

NPL.key_laws: National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy 2082 (2025), Election Code of Conduct 2082 (2026), National Advertising Policy 2026, Individual Privacy Act 2075 (2018), E-commerce Act 2081 (2025)

NLD.name: Netherlands

regulation.binding_note: The EU AI Act is the single AI-specific binding instrument in force; the Dutch implementing act remains a draft after its April-June 2026 consultation.
regulation.summary: The directly applicable EU AI Act governs AI in the Netherlands, with prohibited-practice and AI literacy rules applying since February 2025, general-purpose AI obligations since August 2025, and high-risk obligations deferred to December 2027 and August 2028 by the Digital Omnibus on AI that entered into force on 27 July 2026. National implementation is incomplete: the Uitvoeringswet AI-verordening, which designates the market surveillance authorities, penalties and the joint regulatory sandbox, closed consultation on 1 June 2026 and has not been enacted. Beyond the AI Act, the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens' Directorate for Coordination of Algorithms exercises algorithm-specific oversight under the GDPR and the UAVG.

promotion.note: AiNed/Growth Fund AI programmes, a €71.7 million AI factories commitment (January 2026) and the Nationaal AI Deltaplan are funded, while the joint AI regulatory sandbox awaits the implementing act.

NLD.key_laws: EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) (2024), Digital Omnibus on AI amending the AI Act (2026), General Data Protection Regulation (2018), Dutch GDPR Implementation Act / UAVG (2018), Uitvoeringswet AI-verordening draft bill (2026, in consultation), Nationaal AI Deltaplan (2025), Government Algorithm Register policy (2022)

NZL.name: New Zealand

regulation.binding_note: Binding levers are general law only: Privacy Act 2020, Biometric Processing Privacy Code and Customer and Product Data Act 2025, none written for AI systems.
regulation.summary: New Zealand regulates AI through existing law and voluntary frameworks: the July 2025 Strategy for Artificial Intelligence: Investing with Confidence, the Algorithm Charter for Aotearoa New Zealand and the Public Service AI Framework carry no legal force, while the only binding rules touching AI are the Privacy Act 2020, the Privacy Amendment Act 2025 (IPP3A from 1 May 2026) and the Biometric Processing Privacy Code, which became fully applicable to pre-existing biometric processing on 3 August 2026. The one AI-specific legislative proposal, the Deepfake Digital Harm and Exploitation Bill, passed first reading and received submissions to 19 June 2026 but lapsed when Parliament was dissolved on 1 October 2026 ahead of the 7 November election.

promotion.note: Funded programmes include up to $70 million for AI research via the New Zealand Institute for Advanced Technology, the R&D Tax Incentive and a 2026 small-business AI adoption pilot, with no AI…

NZL.key_laws: Privacy Act 2020, Algorithm Charter for Aotearoa New Zealand (2020), Public Service AI Framework (2025), New Zealand's Strategy for Artificial Intelligence: Investing with Confidence (2025), Responsible AI Guidance for Businesses (2025), Responsible AI Guidance for the Public Service: GenAI (2025), Privacy Amendment Act 2025, Biometric Processing Privacy Code 2025, Customer and Product Data Act 2025, Deepfake Digital Harm and Exploitation Bill (2025, lapsed on dissolution of Parliament in October 2026)

NIC.name: Nicaragua

regulation.summary: As of mid-2026, Nicaragua has no binding AI-specific legislation, no draft AI bill under formal legislative consideration, and no AI-focused executive orders in force. The only AI-relevant activity was a June 2023 National Assembly task force agreement to develop proposals, which produced no enacted instrument; existing laws such as the Special Cybercrime Law (No. 1042, 2020) and the National Cybersecurity Strategy 2020–2025 touch digital activity incidentally but contain no AI provisions.

NIC.key_laws: Special Law on Cybercrimes No. 1042 (2020), National Cybersecurity Strategy 2020–2025 (Presidential Decree No. 24-2020)

NER.name: Niger

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: Loi n° 2017-28 (amended by Loi n° 2019-71) on personal data and the cybercrime framework, with no AI-specific binding instrument.
regulation.summary: Niger has no AI-specific legislation, no draft AI bill and no adopted national AI strategy; the Ministry of Communication, Posts and Digital Economy announced at the second Semaine de l'Intelligence Artificielle et des Technologies Géospatiales in July 2025 that a national AI and geospatial strategy would be elaborated through an inclusive process, and no such instrument has been published. AI-related activity falls under general instruments, chiefly Loi n° 2017-28 of 3 May 2017 on personal data protection as amended by Loi n° 2019-71, which is not written for AI. The country remains under military rule following the July 2023 coup, with the Charter of Refoundation replacing the suspended constitutional order.

promotion.note: AI activity is limited to the ANSI-organised SIATeG week with hackathon and donor-funded training; no national AI fund, procurement rule or sandbox exists.

NER.key_laws: Loi n° 2017-28 du 3 mai 2017 relative à la protection des données à caractère personnel, amended by Loi n° 2019-71 (2019); Niger 2.0 digital strategy (2017). No AI-specific law, regulation or national AI strategy has been adopted.

NGA.name: Nigeria

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument applies: Chapter Five of the NITDA Internet Code of Practice 2026 governing AI use by internet access service providers.
regulation.summary: Nigeria has no standalone AI law: the National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill, which would give NITDA risk-tiered powers over AI systems, was still in the legislative process in mid-2026, and separate National Artificial Intelligence Commission and Nigerian Artificial Intelligence bills remain at committee stage. Binding AI-specific obligations exist only in narrow instruments — Chapter Five of the NITDA Internet Code of Practice 2026 for internet access service providers and the 2025 Guidelines for Clearance of IT Projects covering federal procurement of AI-enabled systems valued at NGN 10 million or more. The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and its General Application and Implementation Directive 2025 carry the bulk of practical AI oversight as general law.

promotion.note: 3MTT skills funding, the National AI Research Scheme, the N-ATLAS language model and AI procurement clearance exist, but the National Regulatory Sandbox only had its Technical Working Group…

PRK.name: North Korea

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument is in force; general technology and information security statutes contain no AI provisions.
regulation.summary: North Korea has no AI-specific legislation, regulation or formal governance instrument. Technology is governed through general sectoral statutes — the Science and Technology Law, the Law on the Introduction of New Technology (revised 2026), the Information Security Law, the Telecommunications Law and the Electronic Authentication Law — none of which contains provisions written for AI systems, while the 2026-2030 Five-Year Plan adopted at the Ninth Workers' Party Congress in February 2026 lists information technology and AI as development priorities.

promotion.note: The 2026-2030 Five-Year Plan announced at the Ninth Party Congress in February 2026 prioritises AI, with no published funding program, procurement rule or sandbox.

PRK.key_laws: Five-Year Plan for National Economic Development 2026-2030 (2026, names information technology and artificial intelligence as priority areas), Law on the Introduction of New Technology (revised 2026), Science and Technology Law, Information Security Law

NOR.name: Norway

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI today: the Personal Data Act 2018 implementing the GDPR, applied to AI by Datatilsynet.
regulation.summary: Norway has no AI-specific binding instrument in force. The draft KI-loven, which would make the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) applicable through a reference provision, completed public consultation in autumn 2025 with close to 150 responses, but entry into force originally targeted for late summer 2026 has slipped: the government will consult on the EU simplification package in autumn 2026 and present a bill in spring 2027, and the EEA Joint Committee has not yet incorporated the Regulation. The new Public Administration Act adopted 20 June 2025 contains binding rules on automated decisions and documentation of decision logic for public bodies, but no commencement date has been set.

promotion.note: Datatilsynet's regulatory sandbox operates with NOK 6 million earmarked in its 2026 letter of allocation and KI-Norge received NOK 30 million, while AI-specific procurement rules are absent.

OMN.name: Oman

regulation.binding_note: Royal Decree No. 50/2026 establishing the Artificial Intelligence Special Zone is the single binding AI-titled instrument, in force since May 2026.
regulation.summary: Oman regulates AI through the General Policy for the Safe and Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence Systems, issued by the Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology on 1 April 2025 and effective 9 April 2025, a risk-based policy instrument rather than a statute. Royal Decree No. 50/2026 of 30 April 2026 is binding and AI-titled but establishes an Artificial Intelligence Special Zone in Muscat Governorate under the Law of Special Economic Zones and Free Zones rather than imposing duties on AI systems. General law, principally the Personal Data Protection Law (Royal Decree 6/2022), reaches AI processing without containing provisions written for AI.

promotion.note: The National Programme for Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Digital Technologies funds AI initiatives and Royal Decree 50/2026 grants tax and investment incentives in the AI Special Zone.

PAK.name: Pakistan

regulation.binding_note: Only general law applies to AI: Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 (amended 2025) and the Digital Nation Pakistan Act 2025, neither containing AI-specific obligations.
regulation.summary: Pakistan has no binding AI legislation; the National AI Policy 2025, the Islamabad AI Declaration 2026 and the National Data Governance Policy 2026 are executive policy documents, and the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Bill 2024 remains in Senate committee. AI-specific duties on transparency, human review of automated decisions and generative-AI controls apply only to federal public bodies through policy, while private-sector AI is touched only incidentally by the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 as amended in 2025. No personal data protection statute has been enacted.

promotion.note: National AI Fund, Ignite-financed AI programmes and AI Centres of Excellence operate under the National AI Policy 2025; the State Bank of Pakistan sandbox is financial, not AI-specific.

PLW.name: Palau

regulation.binding_note: Executive Order No. 500 (April 2026) creating the Office of Applied Technology and Strategy covers government technology with AI use cited as a theme, but no binding AI-specific rule exists.
regulation.summary: Palau has no statute, regulation, executive order or national strategy whose subject is artificial intelligence. AI falls only under general instruments such as the Privacy Act provisions of the Palau National Code and the Cybersecurity Act passed by the Olbiil Era Kelulau on 20 July 2026, neither of which contains AI-specific provisions, and no competent authority for AI exists.

promotion.note: No AI funding scheme, AI procurement rule or regulatory sandbox exists; AI activity is confined to Palau Small Business Development Center training sessions for entrepreneurs.

PAN.name: Panama

regulation.binding_note: The only binding texts reaching AI are Executive Decree 36 of 2026, which creates coordination bodies, and general Law 81 of 2019 on data protection.
regulation.summary: Panama has no binding AI law imposing obligations on AI systems; the unified Bill 588 establishing adaptive AI governance, based on risk management and regulatory experimentation, passed first debate on 15 April 2026 and remains in committee, while Anteproyecto 51 of 2026 would add Penal Code penalties for malicious AI-generated content. General instruments — Law 81 of 2019 on personal data protection and Law 144 of 2020 on government digital transformation — remain the operative rules touching AI.

promotion.note: The National Advanced Technologies Agenda launched 30 July 2026 carries USD 105 million for the semiconductor strategy plus SENACYT scholarship and training programs; no AI regulatory sandbox…

regulation.summary: Papua New Guinea has no dedicated AI legislation, no AI-specific binding instruments proposed or enacted as of mid-2026. PRY.name: Paraguay

regulation.binding_note: Corte Suprema Resolución N° 12.677/2026 binds judicial actors on AI use; Resolución DINAVISA N° 047/2026 governs AI use inside the health regulator.
regulation.summary: Paraguay has no cross-sector AI statute; a Senate bill regulating and promoting AI systems, which would create an AI regulatory authority, has been socialised in public hearing but not enacted. Binding AI-specific texts in force are institutional: Corte Suprema de Justicia Resolución N° 12.677/2026 on AI use in the judiciary and Resolución DINAVISA N° 047/2026 creating an AI unit in health regulation. Ley N° 7593/2025 on personal data protection grants rights against automated and semi-automated individual decisions and profiling, but takes effect only in November 2027.

promotion.note: Decreto N° 5306/2026 adopts AI, cloud and data-centre industries as sectoral public policy with a special 15-year electricity tariff, and MITIC runs a Taiwan-partnered sovereign AI compute pilot.

PER.name: Peru

regulation.binding_note: Law No. 31814, Supreme Decree No. 115-2025-PCM and Law No. 32314 (2025, AI as a criminal aggravating factor) are in force, with parts of the Reglamento not yet applicable.
regulation.summary: Peru governs AI through Law No. 31814 (2023) and its implementing Reglamento, Supreme Decree No. 115-2025-PCM, which took effect in January 2026 and imposes risk classification, algorithmic transparency, human oversight, internal policies and traceability registers on developers and deployers. promotion.note: The Reglamento and ENIA provide for a national AI sandbox, the Plataforma Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial and CNIDIA, none of which is operating yet.

PHL.name: Philippines

regulation.binding_note: Two AI-specific binding instruments are in force: COMELEC Resolution No. 11064 (2024) and DICT-CSC Joint Memorandum Circular No. 003, Series of 2026.
regulation.summary: The Philippines has no enacted horizontal AI statute; about 40 House bills and 7 Senate bills in the 20th Congress, including House Bill 7396 and Senate Bill 25 (Artificial Intelligence Regulation Act), are being consolidated by a House technical working group into a risk-based Artificial Intelligence Development and Regulation Act. promotion.note: Funded programs include the Center for AI Research (2024), the DOST-led National AI Center for Research and Innovation launched 26 February 2026, and the AI+ Infrastructure Masterplan 2026-2033…

POL.name: Poland

regulation.binding_note: Two AI-specific binding instruments apply: Regulation 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, and the Act of 3 July 2026 on AI Systems whose enforcement chapters start 28 October 2026.
regulation.summary: Poland combines the directly applicable EU AI Act, as amended by the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744), with its own Act of 3 July 2026 on Artificial Intelligence Systems, published 27 July 2026 and in force since 11 August 2026. Coverage is horizontal and AI-specific, but the national supervision, inspection and penalty chapters apply only from 28 October 2026 and the AI Act's high-risk obligations were postponed to December 2027 and August 2028.

promotion.note: The PLN 1 billion Artificial Intelligence Fund, PLLuM/Bielik model programmes and an EuroHPC AI Factory are funded, while the statutory KRiBSI regulatory sandbox is not yet open to applications.

PRT.name: Portugal

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding instrument applies, the EU AI Act as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744; no national AI-specific binding rule exists.
regulation.summary: Portugal has not enacted a dedicated national AI statute and does not plan one; the directly applicable EU AI Act is the regulatory backbone, supplemented by Lei n.º 58/2019 (GDPR implementation), Lei n.º 24/96 (consumer protection), Decreto-Lei n.º 57/2008 and Lei n.º 125/2025 (NIS2). Prohibited-practice, AI-literacy, general-purpose AI and transparency obligations apply, while high-risk obligations were pushed to December 2027 and August 2028 by the Digital Omnibus on AI, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, in force since 27 July 2026. National implementation remains partial: ANACOM acts as market surveillance authority and single point of contact, but national penalty rules and an AI sandbox are outstanding.

promotion.note: ANIA Action Plan 2026-2030, AI Portugal 2030, FCT-funded AMALIA national language model (RCM n.º 178/2026) are funded, with no operating AI regulatory sandbox.

QAT.name: Qatar

regulation.binding_note: Two AI-specific binding instruments apply: the QCB Artificial Intelligence Guideline (2024) and QFC Practice Direction No. 1 of 2026.
regulation.summary: Qatar has no horizontal AI statute; binding rules are the Qatar Central Bank Artificial Intelligence Guideline (September 2024) for licensed financial institutions and QICDRC Practice Direction No. 1 of 2026 governing AI use before the QFC Court and Regulatory Tribunal. The Qatar Financial Markets Authority's draft AI regulations consulted in May 2025 are still unenacted, and the Shura Council on 27 April 2026 referred a proposal for a general debate on AI governance to committee rather than a bill. Everything else — the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2019), MCIT ethical AI principles and NCSA secure-AI guidelines — is non-binding.

promotion.note: The MCIT-QRDI 'Artificial Intelligence for Qatar' (AIQAT) research call opened January 2026, alongside the Fanar Arabic LLM and QFC Digital Assets Lab, with no AI-specific public procurement rules…
