ROU.name: Romania

regulation.binding_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 is the single AI-specific binding instrument; the deepfake labelling bill (PL-x 471/2023) was never promulgated.
regulation.summary: Romania's binding AI rules come entirely from the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), which has applied directly since 1 August 2024 with prohibitions from February 2025, general-purpose AI duties from August 2025 and transparency plus high-risk obligations from 2 August 2026. No standalone domestic AI statute exists: national competent authorities were named by a Government memorandum of 12 March 2026, and the implementing law that would confer control procedures and the national penalty regime remains in preparation. Obligations therefore bind operators across sectors while the domestic supervisory machinery is incomplete.

promotion.note: Funding runs through the National Recovery and Resilience Plan, Digital Europe Programme and European Digital Innovation Hubs; no national AI regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules operate.

ROU.key_laws: EU AI Act / Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (2024), National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024-2027 approved by Government Decision No. 832/2024, MCID Order No. 20484/2023 establishing the Romanian Committee for Artificial Intelligence, Government memorandum of 12 March 2026 designating national competent authorities and the single point of contact for the AI Act, Law No. 190/2018 implementing the GDPR

RUS.name: Russia

regulation.binding_note: Two AI-specific binding acts are in force, Federal Law No. 243-FZ (2026) and Federal Law No. 123-FZ on the Moscow AI experimental legal regime, with part of FZ-243 applying from March 2027.
regulation.summary: Russia moved from strategy to statute with Federal Law No. 243-FZ of 26 July 2026 On Supporting the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies in the Russian Federation, in force since 1 September 2026, which defines artificial intelligence and large foundation models and creates the sovereign and national model statuses. Core obligations - developer duties, machine-readable labelling tools on platforms with over 500,000 daily users, and copyright rules for training - apply only from 1 March 2027, with a transition to 2032 for foreign systems already deployed in sensitive areas. Supporting instruments remain Presidential Decree No. 490 (National AI Strategy to 2030, updated 2024) and the experimental legal regime laws FZ-123 and FZ-258.

promotion.note: The federal AI project within the Economy of Data national programme funds compute and R&D, and experimental legal regimes operate under FZ-258 and FZ-123, while AI procurement rules await…

RUS.key_laws: Federal Law No. 243-FZ On Supporting the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies in the Russian Federation (2026), National Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence until 2030 approved by Presidential Decree No. 490 (2019, updated 2024), Presidential Decree No. 116 establishing the Presidential Commission on the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies (2026), Federal Law No. 123-FZ on the experimental legal regime for artificial intelligence in Moscow (2020, updated 2024), Federal Law No. 258-FZ on experimental legal regimes in the sphere of digital innovation (2020), National Code of Ethics in the Field of Artificial Intelligence (2021)

RWA.name: Rwanda

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: Law No. 058/2021 on personal data protection and Law No. 24/2016 on ICT contain no provision written for AI.
regulation.summary: Rwanda governs AI through a dedicated but non-binding framework: the Cabinet-approved National AI Policy of April 2023, the AI Readiness and Maturity Framework, and RURA's Guidelines on the Ethical Development and Implementation of Artificial Intelligence. Legal effect comes only from general instruments, chiefly Law No. 058/2021 Relating to the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy and Law No. 24/2016 Governing Information and Communication Technologies. The Cabinet decision of 8 June 2026 creating a National Artificial Intelligence Agency moves governance toward institutional form without creating enforceable AI obligations.

promotion.note: Funded programmes include the Rwanda AI Scaling Hub (about RWF 25 billion with Gates Foundation support) and C4IR Rwanda; no AI-specific sandbox or AI procurement rules exist.

RWA.key_laws: National AI Policy (2023), AI Readiness and Maturity Framework for Rwanda (2023), Guidelines on the Ethical Development and Implementation of Artificial Intelligence (RURA), Cabinet decision establishing the National Artificial Intelligence Agency (2026), National Data Sharing Policy (2025), Law No. 058/2021 Relating to the Protection of Personal Data and Privacy, Law No. 24/2016 Governing Information and Communication Technologies

SSD.name: S. Sudan

regulation.binding_note: The binding instruments in force are general: Cybercrime and Computer Misuse Act 2026 and telecom rules of the National Communication Authority, with no AI-specific instrument.
regulation.summary: South Sudan has no AI-specific legislation, draft bill or national AI strategy; the country's first comprehensive digital statute, the Cybercrime and Computer Misuse Act 2026, was signed on 18 February 2026 and addresses hacking, critical infrastructure, online content and investigative powers without any AI provision. A first Data Protection Bill was announced by the Ministry of Information, Communication Technology and Postal Services for 2026 but has not been introduced, and comparative legal reviews place South Sudan as the only East African state with neither AI legislation nor AI soft law.

promotion.note: Officials announced intent to attract AI investment under digital transformation (April 2025) and the National Communication Authority ran an AI app development bootcamp, with no funded program…

SSD.key_laws: Cybercrime and Computer Misuse Act 2026 (signed 18 February 2026), Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Provisional Order 2021, SUDESA Strategic Framework for the Digital Transformation of South Sudan's Government and Public Sector, National Spectrum Management and 5G Strategy (under development, 2026), Data Protection Bill (announced for 2026, not introduced) — none AI-specific

KNA.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: the Consumer Protection Act, 2023 is in force while the Data Protection Act, 2018 remains uncommenced.
regulation.summary: Saint Kitts and Nevis has no AI-specific legislation, no AI bill before the National Assembly, and no national AI strategy. The applicable framework is general technology and consumer law: the Electronic Transactions Act (Cap. 18.44), the Consumer Protection Act, 2023 adopted from the CARICOM model, and the Data Protection Act, 2018, which was passed on 4 May 2018 but has never been commenced. Government statements present consumer protection law as the vehicle for fair and responsible AI, which is the only link between binding law and AI.

promotion.note: Government AI deployments (legal-information assistant launched December 2024, AI traffic management announced November 2024) exist without any AI funding programme, regulatory sandbox or AI…

KNA.key_laws: Data Protection Act, 2018 (passed 4 May 2018, not in force), Electronic Transactions Act (Cap. 18.44, 2011), Consumer Protection Act (2023)

LCA.name: Saint Lucia

regulation.binding_note: Only general law applies, principally the Data Protection Act, Cap 8.18, with no AI-specific binding instrument in force.
regulation.summary: Saint Lucia has no AI-specific legislation, no draft AI bill and no AI provisions inside its general statutes; the partially proclaimed Data Protection Act, Cap 8.18 is the main general instrument that touches automated processing. The Minister for Education and Digital Transformation called in January 2026 for legislation on AI use in school-based assessments, but no text has been introduced. Cullen International's September 2026 regional benchmark confirms that no Caribbean country covered, Saint Lucia included, has adopted an AI-specific regulatory framework.

promotion.note: A cross-sector Regulatory Sandbox for Digital Identity and FinTech, supported by ECLAC, was announced on 15 September 2026; it is not operating and is not AI-specific.

LCA.key_laws: Data Protection Act, Cap 8.18 (2011, partially in force 2023)

VCT.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument is in force, and no regulator decision applying general law to AI has been published.
regulation.summary: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines has no AI-specific legislation, bill or subsidiary regulation; AI is touched only incidentally by the Electronic Transactions Act (2007), Cybercrime Act (2016) and Telecommunications Act (2001), none of which contain a provision written for AI systems. The Privacy Act (2003), which would cover processing of personal data by public authorities, remains un-commenced, leaving no data-protection baseline for automated decision-making.

promotion.note: The World Bank-financed Caribbean Digital Transformation Project funds connectivity and digital skills, with no AI funding line, AI procurement rule or regulatory sandbox.

VCT.key_laws: Electronic Transactions Act (2007), Cybercrime Act (2016), Telecommunications Act (2001), Privacy Act (2003, not in force)

WSM.name: Samoa

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument is in force; the two 2026 national documents are policy and strategy, not regulation.
regulation.summary: Samoa has no dedicated AI legislation, no binding AI rules and no AI bill before the Legislative Assembly. The National Communications & Information Technology Policy 2025/26-2030/31 and the National Cybersecurity Strategy 2025/26-2030/31, launched by the Deputy Prime Minister on 17 April 2026, define artificial intelligence and treat trust, safety and responsible data use as principles, but impose no legal duties. AI activity remains governed incidentally by general instruments including the National Digital Identification Act 2024 and telecommunications law.

promotion.note: MCIT operates no AI funding scheme, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rule; digital spending is infrastructure and digital ID focused.

WSM.key_laws: National Communications & Information Technology Policy Samoa 2025/26-2030/31 (2026), Samoa National Cybersecurity Strategy 2025/26-2030/31 (2026), Pathway for the Development of Samoa 2025/26-2030/31, National Digital Identification Act 2024

SMR.name: San Marino

regulation.binding_note: Law No. 171/2018 (Data Protection Law) is the only binding instrument reaching AI processing; no AI-specific binding instrument exists.
regulation.summary: San Marino has no dedicated AI legislation in force or in the legislative pipeline; AI falls incidentally under Law No. 171/2018 on personal data protection. The Republic signed the Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law on 5 September 2024 as one of its first signatories, but has not ratified it and the treaty remains outside domestic law. The EU–Andorra–San Marino Association Agreement, whose signature and provisional application the Council of the European Union authorised on 16 July 2026, is the channel through which internal-market rules would later reach San Marino.

promotion.note: The high-technology enterprise regime run by San Marino Innovation under Decreto Delegato n. 101/2019, amended by Decreto Delegato n. 91 of 20 July 2026, is technology-generic with no AI funding…

SMR.key_laws: Law No. 171/2018 (Data Protection Law), Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (signed 5 September 2024, not ratified), Decreto Delegato n. 101/2019 on high-technology enterprises as amended by Decreto Delegato n. 91 of 20 July 2026

STP.name: Sao Tome and Principe

regulation.binding_note: The only binding instruments reaching AI are general: Law No. 3/2016 on Personal Data Protection and the Cybercrime Law of 2017.
regulation.summary: São Tomé and Príncipe has no AI-specific legislation, draft bill or sectoral AI rule. The applicable framework is general: Law No. 3/2016 on the Protection of Personal Data, Law No. 7/2017 establishing the National Personal Data Protection Agency (ANPDP), and the Cybercrime Law of 2017, none of which contains provisions written for AI systems. The UNESCO Readiness Assessment Methodology country report places the country at a consumption stage of AI with regulation and oversight identified as a priority still to be addressed.

promotion.note: The World Bank-financed Digital São Tomé and Príncipe project funds connectivity and digital government, with no AI funding line, sandbox or AI procurement rule.

STP.key_laws: Law No. 3/2016 on the Protection of Personal Data (2016), Law No. 7/2017 on the Organisation and Functioning of the National Personal Data Protection Agency (2017), Cybercrime Law (2017), National Cybersecurity Strategy 2024-2028 (2023), UNESCO AI Readiness Assessment Methodology country report for São Tomé and Príncipe (2025)

SAU.name: Saudi Arabia

regulation.binding_note: One binding instrument contains AI-written provisions (Copyright Law 2026 AI-training exception and Implementing Regulations); the PDPL is general law applied to AI.
regulation.summary: Saudi Arabia governs AI mainly through non-binding SDAIA instruments, with binding AI-written provisions confined to the Copyright Law (Royal Decree M/169) in force since 12 August 2026 and its Implementing Regulations, which set conditions on using copyrighted works to develop AI. The Personal Data Protection Law applies to automated processing and profiling without AI-specific duties, and the Draft Responsible AI Policy and Draft Global AI Hub Law remain unenacted after public consultations.

promotion.note: SAMAI national training programme, HUMAIN compute investment, SDAIA Data and Privacy Regulatory Sandbox and the AI Sandbox in Digital Learning (July 2026) operate without codified AI procurement…

SEN.name: Senegal

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: Law No. 2008-12 on personal data protection and Law No. 25/2026 on critical information infrastructures and digital security.
regulation.summary: Senegal has no binding AI-specific legislation; governance rests on the non-binding Stratégie Nationale pour le Développement de l'Intelligence Artificielle (2023) and the New Deal Technologique Horizon 2034 launched in February 2025. Recent digital legislating has been general rather than AI-written: the National Assembly adopted Law No. 25/2026 on the protection of critical information infrastructures and digital security on 20 August 2026, and Law No. 2008-12 on personal data remains the main instrument the regulator applies to AI processing. A regional parliamentary workshop on AI regulation hosted in Dakar from 16 to 18 September 2026 discussed future rules without producing a national bill.

promotion.note: The New Deal Technologique Horizon 2034 commits about USD 1.7 billion across 12 programmes and 50 projects including AI, with no operating AI sandbox or AI procurement rules.

SRB.name: Serbia

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI, principally the Law on Personal Data Protection (2018); no AI-specific binding instrument exists.
regulation.summary: Serbia has no binding AI law in force; artificial intelligence is governed by the Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence 2025-2030, the 2023 Ethical Guidelines for reliable and responsible AI, and general legislation on personal data protection, electronic commerce and information security. A working group of the Ministry of Science, Technological Development and Innovation is drafting a first Law on Artificial Intelligence closely modelled on the EU AI Act, providing risk classification, prohibited practices, labelling of AI-generated content, an Artificial Intelligence Agency and a register of high-risk systems; adoption is targeted for December 2026 and the draft has not been submitted to the National Assembly. A draft Law on Personal Data Protection published for consultation on 30 July 2026 would add AI-specific duties, including mandatory impact assessments and prior opinions for high-risk AI processing, but remains a draft.

promotion.note: State funding supports the Institute for Artificial Intelligence of Serbia, the national AI computing platform and Fund for Science AI calls, while the regulatory sandbox foreseen in the AI Strategy…

SRB.key_laws: Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in the Republic of Serbia 2025-2030 (Official Gazette RS No. 5/2025), Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in the Republic of Serbia 2020-2025 (Official Gazette RS No. 73/2019), Ethical Guidelines for the Development, Application and Use of Reliable and Responsible Artificial Intelligence (2023), Law on Personal Data Protection (2018), Draft Law on Artificial Intelligence (2026, in preparation), Draft Law on Personal Data Protection (2026, public consultation 30 July-10 September 2026)

SYC.name: Seychelles

regulation.binding_note: Only general law binds, principally the Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 24 of 2023); no AI-specific binding instrument exists.
regulation.summary: Seychelles has no dedicated AI legislation and no AI bill in the National Assembly; the Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 24 of 2023), in force since 22 December 2023 and enforced by the Information Commission, reaches AI only as general data law. The single AI-specific instrument is the National Artificial Intelligence in Education Framework 2026-2030, published in March 2026 and approved by Cabinet on 22 July 2026, a non-binding policy limited to state schools that sets expectations on data privacy, child protection, academic integrity, cybersecurity and procurement. The National Institute of Science, Technology and Innovation Act, 2025 (Act 24 of 2025) names artificial intelligence among the institute's promotional functions but has not commenced.

promotion.note: No AI funding scheme, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rule exists; the 2026 National Innovation Fair and Innovation Award Scheme are not AI-specific.

SYC.key_laws: National Artificial Intelligence in Education Framework 2026-2030 (2026), Data Protection Act, 2023 (Act 24 of 2023), National Institute of Science, Technology and Innovation Act, 2025 (Act 24 of 2025)

SLE.name: Sierra Leone

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument is in force; the Cyber Security and Crime Act 2021 addresses cybercrime without AI provisions.
regulation.summary: Sierra Leone has no enacted AI-specific legislation and none before Parliament. The Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation, with the World Bank Group, produced a Draft Sierra Leone AI Readiness Diagnostic Report and held three days of stakeholder consultation in May 2026 toward a first National AI Strategy, which remains unadopted. AI-adjacent conduct falls under general law such as the Cyber Security and Crime Act 2021, and a Cabinet-approved National Data Protection Policy (April 2026) awaits a merged data protection and access-to-information law.

promotion.note: The US$50 million World Bank-funded Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project funds the AI readiness work, the deepfake campaign and AI literacy training for 1,000 civil servants.

SGP.name: Singapore

regulation.binding_note: One AI-specific binding statute is in force, the Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising) (Amendment) Act 2024, alongside general statutes such as the Personal Data Protection Act 2012.
regulation.summary: Singapore governs AI mainly through voluntary, AI-explicit instruments—the Model AI Governance Framework family, AI Verify, and the National AI Strategy Update of 20 May 2026—with binding obligations confined to AI-generated content under the Elections (Integrity of Online Advertising) (Amendment) Act 2024 and the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act 2025. The Personal Data Protection Act 2012 supplies the general legal base, now read through the PDPC Advisory Guidelines on Use of Personal Data in Generative AI, which make AI-specific notification mandatory. The MAS Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Risk Management are still in preparation following the consultation that closed on 31 January 2026.

promotion.note: Four National AI Missions and a S$1 billion National AI R&D commitment, FSTI AIDA grants, Enterprise Innovation Scheme AI deductions and the MAS FinTech Regulatory Sandbox operate without published…

SVK.name: Slovakia

regulation.binding_note: Two AI-specific binding instruments apply: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and Act No. 56/2018 Coll. as amended by Act No. 318/2025 Coll.
regulation.summary: Slovakia is covered by the directly applicable EU AI Act, whose prohibitions, AI-literacy and general-purpose AI duties already apply and whose Article 50 transparency rules apply from 2 August 2026, while Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 postponed high-risk obligations to December 2027. Nationally, Act No. 56/2018 Coll. on conformity assessment of products was amended by Act No. 318/2025 Coll. from 1 January 2026 to anchor AI Act enforcement and penalties, and the Act on State Administration in the Field of Artificial Intelligence and European Data Regulation, approved by the government on 26 August 2026, is in second reading with effect from 1 January 2027. No standalone Slovak AI statute is yet in force.

promotion.note: European Digital Innovation Hubs and national HPC/AI compute projects are funded; the regulatory sandbox exists only in the bill before parliament and no AI procurement rules are adopted.

(2025), Draft Act on State Administration in the Field of Artificial Intelligence and European Data Regulation (2026), Act No. 18/2018 Coll. on Personal Data Protection (2018), Act No. 69/2018 Coll. on Cybersecurity (2018), Government Plenipotentiary for Artificial Intelligence (2025), Action Plan for Digital Transformation of Slovakia 2023–2026 (2023), CERAI Standing Commission on Ethics and Regulation of Artificial Intelligence (2020)

SVN.name: Slovenia

regulation.binding_note: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, ZIUDHPUI and the Media Act ZMed-1 AI-labelling provisions are in force, with the AI Act's high-risk chapter not yet applicable.
regulation.summary: Slovenia regulates AI through directly applicable Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and the national Act on the Implementation of the EU Regulation on Harmonised Rules on Artificial Intelligence (ZIUDHPUI), in force since 21 November 2025, which designates competent authorities, offences and fines. Prohibited practices, general-purpose AI, penalty and Article 50 transparency provisions apply, while high-risk obligations were postponed to 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I) by the Digital Omnibus Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. Sector-specific AI duties exist in the Media Act (ZMed-1, 2025), which requires visible labelling of generative-AI media content and places AI-assisted content under editorial responsibility.

promotion.note: NpUI funding of EUR 112 million, the Slovenian AI Factory with a new supercomputer and the AI Competence Centre operate, while the AKOS regulatory sandbox was still selecting its thematic area until…

SVN.key_laws: EU AI Act / Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (2024), Digital Omnibus on Artificial Intelligence – Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (2026), Act on the Implementation of the EU Regulation on Harmonised Rules on Artificial Intelligence – ZIUDHPUI (2025), Media Act – ZMed-1 (2025), National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence until 2030 – NsUI 2030 (2026), National Programme to Promote the Development and Use of AI in the Republic of Slovenia by 2025 – NpUI (2021), Digital Slovenia 2030 Strategy (2023)

SLB.name: Solomon Islands

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument is in force, and no comprehensive data protection statute exists to apply to AI.
regulation.summary: Solomon Islands has no AI-specific legislation, regulation or bill; AI appears only in planning documents, namely the SIG ICT Services Digital - Data, People, Technology and Cyber Strategy 2026-2030, which lists an AI for Government project and an intention to develop ethical AI guidelines, and the ICT for Education Master Plan 2026-2030 launched by the Ministry of Education and Human Resources Development. The Data Protection and Privacy Bill drafted with UNCTAD support remains unenacted, leaving even general data law absent.

promotion.note: AI for Government is listed as a project in the SIG ICT Services Digital Strategy 2026-2030 with no disbursed AI funding, procurement rule or sandbox.

SLB.key_laws: SIG ICT Services Digital - Data, People, Technology and Cyber Strategy 2026-2030, Solomon Islands ICT for Education Master Plan 2026-2030, National Cyber Security Policy (2024), National ICT Policy (2017), draft Data Protection and Privacy Bill (2024)

SOM.name: Somalia

regulation.binding_note: Only general law applies to AI: the Data Protection Act (Law No. 005 of 2023) and the Communications Act (2017).
regulation.summary: Somalia has no AI-specific legislation, draft bill or national AI strategy; artificial intelligence reaches the statute book only through the Data Protection Act (Law No. 005 of 2023), whose Article 23 gives a right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing and whose transparency duties cover automated decision-making and profiling. Governmental engagement with AI is confined to convening activity, principally the National Communications Authority's AI Summit Somalia 2026 in Mogadishu, which discussed AI governance and regulation without producing a binding instrument.

promotion.note: No AI funding scheme, sandbox or AI procurement rule exists; the World Bank SCALE-UP project financed the June 2026 AI summit only.

SOM.key_laws: Data Protection Act (Law No. 005 of 2023), Communications Act (2017)

ZAF.name: South Africa

regulation.binding_note: POPIA (Act 4 of 2013) is the only binding instrument reaching AI, and it contains no AI-specific provision.
regulation.summary: South Africa has no AI-specific binding legislation. The Draft South Africa National Artificial Intelligence Policy, gazetted on 10 April 2026 with a 60-day comment period, was withdrawn after fictitious AI-generated citations were found, and Minister Solly Malatsi confirmed in September 2026 that a revised draft will reach Cabinet by the end of the 2026/27 financial year. Governance of AI therefore rests on general law, principally the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) and its automated decision-making provision, plus the Electoral Commission's July 2026 draft code requiring labelling of AI-generated campaign content.

promotion.note: The Artificial Intelligence Institute of South Africa, launched by DCDT with the University of Johannesburg and Tshwane University of Technology, runs funded hubs; no AI procurement rules or AI…

ZAF.key_laws: Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) No. 4 of 2013 (fully effective 2021), National AI Policy Framework (2024), National AI Government Summit Discussion Document (2024), Draft South Africa National Artificial Intelligence Policy (gazetted 10 April 2026, withdrawn 2026), Electoral Commission Draft Code of Conduct on Disinformation and AI-generated election content (2026)

KOR.name: South Korea

regulation.binding_note: AI Basic Act and Decree, Public Official Election Act deepfake ban, Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment of Sexual Crimes deepfake offences and amended PIPA AI-training provisions all bind…
regulation.summary: South Korea regulates AI through the Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Establishment of a Foundation for Trustworthiness, in force since 22 January 2026 with its Enforcement Decree, covering high-impact AI in ten designated domains, generative AI transparency, high-performance AI above 10^26 FLOPs and foreign providers via a domestic representative duty whose filings fall due in October 2026. promotion.note: Genesis Mission (over $5 billion announced July 2026), NAIRR and AI procurement rules operate, while the federal AI regulatory sandbox remains only a bill (SANDBOX Act, S.2750).

URY.name: Uruguay

regulation.binding_note: Decreto 276/025 is the single binding instrument whose subject matter expressly includes artificial intelligence projects.
regulation.summary: Uruguay has no comprehensive AI statute; binding AI-relevant rules consist of Articles 74 and 75 of Law 20.212 (2023), which mandate a national data and AI strategy, and Decreto 276/025 of December 2025, which sets a governance scheme with impact assessments, time limits and supervision for controlled testing environments and data spaces used for data and AI projects. The Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence, signed in September 2025, has not been ratified and the treaty itself is not in force. Personal data processing by AI is covered by Law 18.331 (2008), which contains no AI-specific provision.

promotion.note: Uruguay Innova, ANII funding and the Instituto Vidart AI centre opened in September 2026 operate alongside the sandbox launched in 2026, while no AI-specific public procurement rules exist.

URY.key_laws: Law 18.331 Personal Data Protection Law (2008), Law 20.212 Articles 74 and 75 (2023), Decreto 276/025 regulating controlled testing environments and data spaces for data and artificial intelligence (2025), National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024-2030, Agesic AI Regulatory Recommendations (2024), Council of Europe Framework Convention on Artificial Intelligence and Human Rights, Democracy and the Rule of Law (signed September 2025), Artificial Intelligence Strategy for Digital Government (2020)

UZB.name: Uzbekistan

regulation.binding_note: Law No. ZRU-1115 and Ethical Rules No. 3787 are in force, alongside Presidential Decree No. PF-189 of 22 October 2025 whose AI procurement rules apply from 1 June 2026.
regulation.summary: Uzbekistan regulates AI through Law No. ZRU-1115 of 21 January 2026, which defines artificial intelligence, bans legally significant decisions taken solely by AI, requires labelling of AI-generated content and adds administrative fines for unlawful AI-based personal data processing, and through the Ethical Rules for the Creation, Implementation and Use of AI-Based Solutions (Order No. 3787, registered 14 March 2026, in force 17 June 2026), which bind every developer, implementer and user of AI in any sector. The framework is horizontal and principle-based rather than risk-tiered: it contains no high-risk classification, conformity assessment or registration regime, and the national AI standards foreseen by the Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies until 2030 have not been issued.

promotion.note: Presidential Resolution PP-320 of 30 October 2025 allocates $100 million for AI projects and PF-189 sets direct AI procurement and tax incentives, with no AI regulatory sandbox operating.

VUT.name: Vanuatu

regulation.binding_note: Binding tools are general digital statutes, the Digital Transformation Act No. 42 of 2025 and Data Protection and Privacy Act No. 13 of 2024; no AI-specific instrument exists.
regulation.summary: Vanuatu regulates AI through general digital law rather than a dedicated AI instrument: the Digital Transformation Act No. 42 of 2025 names "artificial intelligence (AI) and AI-related data services" as a permit category and gives the Department of Communications and Digital Transformation a statutory function to develop and enforce AI frameworks, while the Data Protection and Privacy Act No. 13 of 2024 grants a right not to be subject to solely automated decisions. Coverage is confined to licensing and data protection, with no high-risk, transparency or conformity obligations. Implementing permit regulations, guidance and an operational enforcement body are absent.

promotion.note: DCDT's Digital Transformation Priority Initiatives and ICT Policy 2025 contain no AI funding program, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rule.

VAT.name: Vatican City

regulation.binding_note: Decree No. DCCII is the single AI-specific binding instrument listed in the Vatican City State Normativa Generale.
regulation.summary: Vatican City State regulates AI through one dedicated binding instrument, Decree No. DCCII of the Pontifical Commission (adopted 16 December 2024, in force 1 January 2025), which defines AI, sets principles of human dignity, transparency and data protection, prohibits discriminatory, manipulative and dignity-violating uses, assigns authorship of AI-generated content to the Governorate, and creates a five-member AI Commission. Coverage is institutional rather than horizontal: it binds the Governorate and Vatican City State bodies, not the whole Roman Curia or private actors. The promised follow-up laws and implementing regulations do not appear in the Governorate's published legislation, and the May 2026 encyclical Magnifica Humanitas carries doctrinal rather than civil-law force.

promotion.note: No AI funding program, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rule exists in Vatican City State's published legislation or Governorate announcements.

VEN.name: Venezuela

regulation.binding_note: No AI-specific binding instrument is in force, and no regulator has applied the Special Law Against Cybercrimes (2001) or other general law to AI systems.
regulation.summary: Venezuela's AI framework rests on a bill and a ministerial ethics code rather than enacted law: the Proyecto de Ley de Inteligencia Artificial cleared first discussion on 19 November 2024, creating a risk classification and a national AI agency, but has not advanced to second discussion. The Ministry of Science and Technology published the Código de Ética para el Desarrollo y Aplicación Responsable de la Inteligencia Artificial on 19 February 2026, setting nine guiding principles without legal force. Binding obligations on AI systems do not exist in any sector.

promotion.note: MINCYT reports a Plan Nacional de Inteligencia Artificial with 65 projects and compute infrastructure work with CANTV, with no disbursement figures, regulatory sandbox or AI procurement rules…

VNM.name: Vietnam

regulation.binding_note: Law 134/2025/QH15, Decree 142/2026/ND-CP and Decision 33/2026/QD-TTg are in force, with their principal obligations still inside transition periods.
regulation.summary: Vietnam governs AI through a dedicated horizontal statute, Law No. 134/2025/QH15, in force since 1 March 2026, with a three-tier risk classification, prohibited practices, transparency and deepfake labelling duties, and registration of medium- and high-risk systems through the national one-stop AI portal. Implementing detail arrived with Decree No. 142/2026/ND-CP (effective 1 May 2026) and the Prime Minister's high-risk list in Decision No. 33/2026/QD-TTg (effective 15 August 2026), covering 46 system types across six sectors. Full application is still phased: general compliance deadlines fall on 1 March 2027 and 1 September 2027 for healthcare, education and finance, and the administrative-sanctions decree has not been issued.

promotion.note: Decree 142/2026/ND-CP establishes a controlled AI sandbox with approval procedures alongside Decree 353/2025/ND-CP digital-technology sandbox and National AI Strategy funding, with no AI procurement…

regulation.binding_note: No binding instrument of any kind addresses AI; Yemen also lacks a comprehensive data protection statute that regulators could apply to AI.
regulation.summary: Yemen has no dedicated AI law, national AI strategy or AI regulator, and neither the internationally recognised government in Aden nor the de facto authority in Sana'a has published an AI framework. Digital policy activity is limited to the National Cybersecurity Strategy approved in January 2023, the March 2025 Strategic Orientation towards Digital Transformation Project of the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology, and a still-unenacted draft law on combating information technology crimes, none of which addresses AI systems. Armed conflict and parallel institutions leave AI unregulated.

promotion.note: No AI funding program, procurement rule or regulatory sandbox exists; activity is limited to occasional public-sector AI training courses such as the April 2026 course on AI in administrative and…

ZMB.name: Zambia

regulation.binding_note: Only general law reaches AI: Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021, Cyber Security Act No. 3 of 2025 and Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025.
regulation.summary: Zambia's AI framework rests on the non-binding National Artificial Intelligence Strategy launched by the Ministry of Technology and Science in November 2024, which sets pillars on policy and regulation, skills, infrastructure, research and sectoral adoption and calls for a National AI Policy, a National AI Council and technical working groups. No AI-specific binding instrument exists or is before Parliament; AI-related conduct falls under the Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 and the Cyber Security Act No. 3 of 2025 and Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025, which replaced the Cyber Security and Cyber Crimes Act of 2021 and contain no provisions written for AI systems.

promotion.note: The strategy announces an Emerging Technologies Centre of Excellence and AI innovation support, with no disbursed AI funding programme, AI procurement rules or operating regulatory sandbox.

ZWE.name: Zimbabwe

regulation.binding_note: Only general law binds — the Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] (2021) and the 2024 Licensing of Data Controllers Regulations.
regulation.summary: Zimbabwe governs AI through the non-binding National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026–2030, approved by Cabinet in October 2025 and launched by President Mnangagwa at Parliament on 13 March 2026. The strategy's Pillar 4 promises a National AI Act with a risk-based framework and national AI technical standards, but no AI bill has been drafted or tabled. Binding obligations touching AI come only from the Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] (2021) and its 2024 licensing regulations, which address personal data generally.

promotion.note: The Mugove/Umqele/Isabelo co-investment fund, Project Pangolin data platform and the Innovation Crucible regulatory sandbox are announced in the strategy and not yet operating.
